detail.abstract: Rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields are often treated as direct evidence that yen-funded carry trades are becoming uneconomic and that Japanese capital will return from foreign assets. That interpretation conflates curve location, relative currency sensitivity, and aggregate balance-sheet adjustment. This paper separates a daily short-end proxy from an orthogonalized long-duration innovation over January 2013-July 2026 and estimates transmission through predetermined BIS yen-credit and IMF portfolio-holdings gradients. The primary sample contains eight practically tradable currencies; four managed, restricted, or disrupted currencies enter only an extended sample. Hierarchical interaction models include the time-varying exposure levels, and 999 moving-block replications re-estimate both stages of long-duration inference. The primary linear short-end gradients are statistically equivalent to economically negligible effects at H0, H1, and H5. Directional exposure and average-carry estimates remain inconclusive. Positive-shock high-volatility amplification survives an expanded fifteen-test Holm family at H1, while the direct positive-minus-negative volatility contrast survives its three-horizon family at H5. These results do not coincide at a common horizon and therefore cannot satisfy the paper's joint carry-unwind rule. The sole full-family rejection is also sensitive to expanding the family from 18 to 19 tests. Long-duration gradients and weekly local projections through eight weeks do not confirm portfolio substitution or later repatriation. The evidence supports limited historical state dependence, but neither a systemic carry unwind nor confirmed capital return.

title: Future Projection: Constructing Believable Organizational Futures under Conditions of Uncertainty

detail.title: Future Projection: Constructing Believable Organizational Futures under Conditions of Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests, personal relationships, or other conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this working paper. The views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a conceptual theoretical work based on analysis of existing scholarly literature and publicly available organizational examples. It did not involve human participants, identifiable personal data, or animal subjects. Accordingly, institutional ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Leadership scholars have long recognized that organizations depend upon leaders to reduce uncertainty by providing direction and articulating a vision for the future. Existing research demonstrates that strategic vision, organizational sensemaking, and future-oriented leadership influence commitment and organizational change, yet comparatively less attention has been devoted to the leadership process through which institutions construct believable interpretations of organizational direction under conditions of uncertainty. This paper examines the relationship between strategic leadership, organizational sensemaking, and future-oriented communication through a conceptual analysis of scholarship on visionary leadership, strategic foresight, organizational change, and institutional interpretation. The analysis identifies a theoretical gap concerning how leaders transform uncertain futures into credible organizational realities that followers are willing to pursue. To address this gap, the paper develops the concept of Future Projection, defined as the leadership process through which institutions construct believable interpretations of organizational direction, continuity, and possibility under conditions of uncertainty. The analysis argues that organizational commitment to future objectives depends not solely upon the existence of strategic plans or visionary leadership but upon the credibility of the narratives through which leaders explain where the organization is going, why that future is attainable, and how followers fit within it. By identifying Future Projection as a distinct leadership mechanism, this paper extends existing scholarship on leadership and organizational change while contributing a foundational construct to Narrative Power Leadership Theory (NPLT). The findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding how leadership narratives shape organizational expectations, strategic continuity, and collective commitment during periods of uncertainty and transformation.

title: Institutional and Network Mechanisms Constraining European Defence-industrial Autonomy

detail.title: Institutional and Network Mechanisms Constraining European Defence-industrial Autonomy

detail.abstract: This study examines the institutional and industrial structure of the defence procurement market in the European Union in the aftermath of the 2022 exogenous demand shock. The sudden and massive surge in demand encountered pronounced inelasticity in domestic supply. The resulting supply-demand gap prompted European governments to enact extensive fiscal stimulus measures-ranging from Germany's establishment of a €100 billion special off-budget fund and Poland's increase of defence appropriations to 4-5% of GDP, to the deployment of supranational regulatory instruments (ASAP, EDIRPA, EDIS, EDIP) and the mobilisation of European Defence Fund resources (~€8 billion). Nevertheless, a substantial portion of the unleashed liquidity failed to capitalise the domestic industrial base as expected, being rechannelled instead toward external contractors. This outcome was driven by a complex set of structural constraints. Structural fragmentation of the industrial base-exemplified by the concurrent operation in the EU of 12 to 14 main battle tank types compared to a single type in the US-precludes the achievement of economies of scale, thereby sustaining high average costs. Concurrently, short time preferences among decision-makers exacerbate principal-agent problems: off-the-shelf procurement systematically outperforms long-term domestic capital investment projects in competitive selection. Interoperability mandates function in this context as covert non-tariff entry barriers. An additional driver of resource reallocation has been institutional capture and rent-seeking by external actors, which facilitated the lowering of the domestic content requirement from 100% to 65% and blurred the criteria defining a 'design authority'. Coupled with information asymmetry perpetuated by revolving doors between the public and private sectors, these conditions resulted in over 70% of total procurement contract value flowing outside the EU (with 60-64% captured by US prime contractors). The industry-standard lifecycle cost structure ('30% platform, 70% sustainment') generates substantial switching costs, cements vendor lock-in, and locks in long-term capital outflows over the 30-to 40-year

title: Corporate Governance and Business Failure Prediction: An Empirical Investigation in Emerging Markets

detail.title: Corporate Governance and Business Failure Prediction: An Empirical Investigation in Emerging Markets

All costs associated with the design, data collection, analysis, and preparation of this manuscript were borne solely by the authors.
declarations.funderStatement: This article has not received any funding and is entirely the responsibility of the author.

detail.abstract: This study empirically investigates the predictive power of corporate governance mechanisms for business failure in an emerging market context. Using a quantitative, descriptive, analytical, and causal research design, the study examines a sample of agricultural firms listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange over the period 2016-2023 (7 years). Data were collected from annual financial statements and accompanying notes available through the Stock Exchange Organization database and Rahavard Novin and Tadbir Pardaz software. The statistical analysis was conducted using Eviews software. The findings reveal that the interactive variable of corporate governance significantly enhances the prediction of business failure, particularly in the presence of accounting anomalies, with a positive coefficient and significance level below 5%, supporting the hypothesis at the 95% confidence level. Control variables including firm size, return on assets, loss-making status, and sales growth exhibit negative and significant relationships with business failure. The model explains approximately 23% of the variance in the dependent variable. These results underscore the critical role of corporate governance mechanisms in mitigating business failure risk and highlight the importance of strengthening governance frameworks in developing economies.

detail.abstract: Research on strategic flexibility and open innovation is growing rapidly in the context of digital transformation yet the relationships among these constructs remain fragmented across different academic streams, This study aims to synthesize existing empirical and theoretical evidence, identify main research trends and uncover critical gaps in the literature. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted across prominent academic databases, including Scopus and Google Scholar, and ResearchGate adhering to rigorous inclusion and exclusion criteria. The screening and selection process ultimately yielded 36 highly relevant studies that directly address the intersections among strategic flexibility and open innovation and digital transformation. The findings reveal clear positive interrelationships among the three constructs. Digital transformation consistently drives open innovation by improving access to external knowledge, enhancing cross-organizational collaboration and breaking down traditional boundaries. Furthermore, strategic flexibility empowers organizations to adapt resources, strategies, and operational processes to environmental shifts, while digital transformation acts as an enabler that strengthens overall organizational flexibility. Despite these advances, the literature remains fragmented, with a distinct lack of integrated empirical frameworks combining strategic flexibility, open innovation, and digital transformation within a unified model.

title: Q-ALU: Quant Asymmetric Leaky Unit: A Market Psychology Aware Activation Function with Downside Risk Protection for High Frequency Quantitative Trading and Deep Reinforcement Learning

detail.title: Q-ALU: Quant Asymmetric Leaky Unit: A Market Psychology Aware Activation Function with Downside Risk Protection for High Frequency Quantitative Trading and Deep Reinforcement Learning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Deep neural networks applied to high frequency trading (HFT) and algorithmic portfolio management frequently suffer from structural inductive mismatch. Prevailing activation functions, including the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU), Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU), and Swish/SiLU, were fundamentally designed for computer vision and natural language processing under the implicit assumption of isotropic, symmetric feature representations. Financial price discovery, however, is inherently asymmetric: downside liquidations and panic cascades occur with substantially greater velocity and severity than bullish accumulation phases, as formalized by Kahneman and Tversky prospect theory. Furthermore, intermediate hidden representations in trading models are severely corrupted by microstructure noise (for example bid ask bounce), leading to rampant overtrading and catastrophic policy collapse in reinforcement learning algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). To resolve these challenges, this paper introduces the Quant Asymmetric Leaky Unit (Q-ALU), a novel activation function custom engineered for financial time series modeling and deep reinforcement learning. Q-ALU couples a dynamic hyperbolic tangent momentum riding regime on the positive domain with an exponential to linear downside barrier on the negative domain. We mathematically prove that Q-ALU is globally monotonic (f ′ (x) ≥ 0 ∀x ∈ R), possesses a C 0 continuous origin, and exhibits a novel Dynamic Gradient Overshoot, delivering a +13.53% sensitivity spike at the critical drawdown threshold x =-2δ before relaxing into linear cut loss tracking. In empirical evaluations on 5,000 out of sample ticks (from a 10,000 tick multi regime stream) under realistic transaction costs (1.0 to 1.5 bps fee per turnover), neural trading policies equipped with Q-ALU achieve an out of sample return of +75.85% with a Per-Step Sortino of 0.142, a Profit Factor of 2.09, and a Maximum Drawdown (MDD) of 2.79%, vastly outperforming baseline architectures utilizing ReLU (+5.43% return, 0.95% MDD) and GELU (+1.42% return, 0.01% MDD). Furthermore, when evaluated across 2,834 real world high frequency market bars of BTC/USDT and implemented within Temporal 1D Convolutional Neural Networks across 5 random seeds, Q-ALU demonstrates consistent alpha generation and superior fee resistance. Finally, we provide numerically stable, production grade PyTorch modules and hardware optimized CUDA C++ kernels achieving up to 133 million evaluations per second.

title: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning with Reliability-aware Client Selection for Heterogeneous Edge Devices

detail.title: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning with Reliability-aware Client Selection for Heterogeneous Edge Devices

detail.abstract: Federated learning is rapidly becoming a key paradigm for deploying machine learning models across distributed edge devices without aggregating raw data to a central server to satisfy emerging regulatory and ethical demands for data privacy. The extension to multimodal settings adds challenges though: modality imbalance, partial trust of the client/limited ability to trust the data/client, limited and variable devices, high privacy risk due to richer data representations. In this article, a structured overview of privacy-preserving multimodal federated learning is shown which focuses on reliable client selection for the settings of heterogeneous edge devices. The review is based on over 50 peer-reviewed or archival sources that are published mainly between 2019 and 2025 and cover four concurrent lines of research: federated optimisation foundational research, privacy-preserving aggregation methods such as differential privacy, secure multiparty computation, and homomorphic encryption, client selection and reliability estimation, and emerging multimodal federated architectures. A proposal for a unified conceptual framework based on reliability scoring, derived from device capabilities, link measurements, historical update fidelity, and hence modality completeness, is introduced that enables flexible learning in the presence of system and statistical heterogeneity, while remaining privacy-preserving. The review also compiles quantitative results from various papers to summarise the compromises required to balance privacy assurance, communication efficiency and model accuracy. Open questions are highlighted, such as the lack of standardized multimodal benchmarks, the computational load on low power devices of cryptographic privacy mechanism, and the challenge of optimising jointly fairness, robustness and efficiency. Finally, the research directions for integrated and reliable multimodal FL systems with privacy protection in real-world FL edge deployments are summarized.

detail.abstract: Frits R. Rosendaal occupies an unusual concentration of authority across scientific publishing and research-integrity governance. He is Editor in Chief of Research Integrity and Peer Review, a senior Leiden/LUMC integrity-committee chair, a member of the Austrian Agency for Research Integrity commission, a leader within LERU's integrity policy work and Vice-Chair of COPE. Multiple appointments do not establish bias or misconduct. They do, however, create recurring disclosure, recusal and role-separation duties. This public-record audit tests whether those duties are externally verifiable. It identifies two 2026 articles in Rosendaal's journal. In one, Rosendaal is a co-author, yet the competing-interests statement declares none and the open peer-review history does not identify the handling editor. In the other, authors discuss a homeopathy case that Rosendaal personally managed for OeAWI; a current journal-board member associated with Retraction Watch reviewed the paper and suggested Retraction Watch sources, while the public record again omits the handling editor. Named, multi-round peer review and a review that challenged accusatory language are significant counterevidence against any allegation of sham review. The supported criticism is therefore not corruption but non-auditability. A separate appearance question arises from Rosendaal's categorical published position on homeopathy before his OeAWI case-management role; the public record does not show whether OeAWI assessed that position under its conflict rule. The article rejects guilt by association, finds no public basis for linking Rosendaal to most named watchdog websites, and proposes mandatory editor-author disclosures, case-level recusal attestations, handling-editor identification, board appointment dates, role registers and independent process audits. Integrity authority is legitimate only when its own exercise can be checked.

title: Responsible Decision-making in Digital Projects: The Power and Limits of Ethical Aids
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Finance, University of Zurich - Department Finance, Fachhochschule Graubünden and University of Applied Sciences of the Grisons - Swiss Institute for Entrepreneurship (SIFE)

detail.title: Responsible Decision-making in Digital Projects: The Power and Limits of Ethical Aids

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Both studies received ethical approval from the authors’ institutional ethics committee
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by Innosuisse (Swiss Innovation Agency) through an innovation project grant (No. 103.382 IP-SBM).

detail.abstract: Digital transformation creates opportunities for organizations but also raises ethical risks related to privacy, surveillance, discrimination, and data use. Corporate digital responsibility (CDR) emphasizes the need to support responsible decision-making when evaluating digital initiatives. One widely used approach involves checking questions that encourage ethical reflection, yet little is known about their effectiveness. Across two experimental studies with professionals involved in data-related activities, we examined two types of checking questions: Ought-Questions, which prompt comparisons with normative standards, and Is-Questions, which direct attention to project-specific ethical risks. Contrary to expectations, Ought-Questions did not reliably reduce the acceptability of ethically problematic digital projects and, under some conditions, produced a boomerang effect. These effects depended on participants’ recognition of normative discrepancies and ethical risks. In contrast, Is-Questions, alone or combined with Ought-Questions, consistently promoted more critical evaluations. The findings show that ethical decision aids can both support and undermine responsible judgments in digital contexts.

detail.abstract: The current study sought to identify the impact of digital leadership on strategic success in Iraqi university institutions. The study was condusted in the colleges of Misan University, where a questionnaire was distributed to a sample of (97) managers, and (89) valid questionnaires were obtained for analysis. The study adopted the descriptive-analytical approach and relied on four dimensions of the independent variable, digital leadership. The study questions were answered through testing a number of hypotheses concerning variance, relationship, and impact using the statistical program (SPSS V.26). The study reached several conclusions, the most important of which is that the dimensions of digital leadership affect strategic success. The study also found a statistically significant correlation between digital leadership, with its dimensions, and strategic success. Furthermore, the results indicated a statistically significant impact of digital leadership, at both the overall level and the level of its dimensions, on strategic success. The study also found variation in the impact of the dimensions of digital leadership on strategic success in the universities under study. The study presented several recommendations to the management of the university under study, the most important of which is the need to deepen attention to digital leadership because of its importance in developing and achieving the objectives of the university institution at the strategic level.

title: Unlearning as a Mechanism of Strategy-as-Practice: Explaining Middle-Manager Strategy Deviation During Prolonged Crisis
affiliations: Anglia Ruskin University, Ulster University - Ulster University and Anglia Ruskin University

detail.title: Unlearning as a Mechanism of Strategy-as-Practice: Explaining Middle-Manager Strategy Deviation During Prolonged Crisis
detail.abstract: Strategy-as-Practice (SAP) research on middle managers, most fully specified by Christie and Tippmann's (2024, Long Range Planning) implementation model, has established which activities carry strategy deviation, but not why deviation occurs. Organisational unlearning theory offers a candidate answer: individual unlearning, the deliberate discarding of obsolete routines and assumptions, is a purposive driver of deviation that has never been examined at the level of SAP activity. Bringing these literatures together, this paper examines how individual middle-manager unlearning is enacted through recognisable SAP activity, and under what conditions it scales into organisational unlearning during sustained disruption. Drawing on a 24-month longitudinal qualitative study of six UK middle managers during the COVID-19 pandemic (48 interviews, contemporaneous communications, and documents), we identify three unlearning mechanisms across temporal phases: discursive de-legitimation, sociomaterial decommissioning, and pattern-breaking praxis. We show that while cooperation and autonomy manage localised or sanctioned workarounds, coalition-building is the activity most likely to carry unlearning into organisational uptake. Where managers relied solely on autonomy, unlearning remained isolated at the individual level because secondary organisational actors did not reciprocate. This study extends SAP research by providing an unlearning-based explanatory logic for strategy deviation, contributes to unlearning theory by specifying the practice mechanisms of individual-to-organisational transmission, and repositions middle managers as the critical site where individual and organisational unlearning intersect

title: Not Every Contradiction Is a Lie: A Falsifiability-Based Test for Distinguishing Structural Tension from Cognitive Projection

detail.title: Not Every Contradiction Is a Lie: A Falsifiability-Based Test for Distinguishing Structural Tension from Cognitive Projection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the developer of Learnable Theory, the framework applied in this paper to Miller's (2026) work on attentional omission. The paper's central claims are evaluated on their theoretical and predictive merits, and the author has no financial or personal relationship with Miller or with any organisation that could be perceived to have influenced the analysis presented here.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a theoretical paper. It did not involve human participants, animal subjects, or the collection of new empirical data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Confidence is a poor guide to whether a claimed contradiction is real. This paper addresses a specific analytic problem: given two apparent contradictions, one between a religious text and a set of encoded prophecies, one between a corporate marketing claim and a car's physical emissions, how can an analyst determine, before further argument is invested, which is a genuine structural tension and which is an artefact of the analyst's own search procedure? The cognitive literature on heuristics and biases (Tversky & Kahneman, 1974) and on apophenia, the disposition to perceive patterns in noise (Conrad, 1958; Kapur, 2003), explains why humans generate spurious contradictions but does not supply a public test for telling a spurious one from a genuine one. This paper applies such a test, Learnable Theory's own three-condition instrument for verifying a claimed Inverse Difference (Magni, Marchetti, & Alharbi, 2023; Magni, 2026), non-contrariety, structural necessity, and observable frame collapse, and grounds each condition independently in an existing external literature, Weick's (1995) account of organisational sensemaking for structural necessity and Goffman's (1974) frame analysis for frame collapse, rather than resting the test on Learnable Theory's own internal consistency alone; the test's underlying logic also draws on Popper's (1959) falsifiability principle without treating falsifiability itself as the paper's subject. The test is applied to two paired cases: the 1994 Bible code controversy, which fails it, and the Volkswagen emissions scandal, analysed through peer-reviewed organisational research (Fey et al., 2023; Rhodes, 2016; Kaptein, 2015), which passes it. The paper argues that both cases share a specific statistical vulnerability, data dredging, and that an active control condition is what strips that vulnerability away in each domain.

title: Post COVID-19 increment of chemical accidents examined by the Markov-chain rule and segmented negative binomial regression
affiliations: Soongsil University - Soongsil University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Soongsil University - Soongsil University

detail.title: Post COVID-19 increment of chemical accidents examined by the Markov-chain rule and segmented negative binomial regression
detail.abstract: Propensities of chemical accidents were examined to estimate the policy and environmental effects including the COVID-19 pandemic using a discrete-time Markov-chain and Segmented regression methods. Despite inhomogeneous dynamics of accident trends, the two significant turning points on July 2016 and March 2023 could be discerned from a dataset provided by the National Institute of Chemical Safety (NICS) in Republic of Korea from 2014 to 2025. The first period of simple moving average of time-dependent profile of chemical accidents appeared to show a ’unstable phase’ with extreme event and political decision by the government regulatory measure of the chemical substances control act until the pre-pandemic era before July, 2016. This was followed by a steady phase involving the COVID-19 pandemic lock-down period until March, 2023. A rising phase is notably observed along with post corona aftermath for the accidents counting up to now mainly attributed to increasing cases of non-compliance of safety standards. A first order Markov chain model was introduced to validate the results by integrating change point detection. Moreover, we fit segmented negative binomial regression into the dataset so that changes on each detected period were qualitatively evaluated, showed an immediate level change of -36.7% in the monthly accident rate following July 2016, and +42.7% following March 2023. This study highlights the necessity of algorithmic determination for interventions to evaluate specific events and policies in affecting domestic chemical accident trends. Our analysis will be helpful to implement prevent measures of industrial accidents in the post-pandemic era.

title: AIRE and AIREOM: A Foundational Framework for Human-AI Strategy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AIRE and AIREOM: A Foundational Framework for Human-AI Strategy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a conceptual thought-leadership framework and does not report research involving human participants, patients, animals, or identifiable case-study subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.

detail.abstract:
This thought-leadership paper introduces a new Human-AI strategy framework for generative AI, LLMs, and agentic AI systems. It focuses on optimizing the AI experience to drive adoption, customer delight, and market expansion. Its foundation is AIRE — AI as Relational Entity — a theory of how advanced language-based, generative, and agentic AI systems come to matter in human cognition, emotion, behavior, and work. The central premise is that the strategic significance of generative AI, LLMs, and agentic AI will not be determined only by what AI systems can produce, automate, or retrieve, but by the relationships users develop with these systems and the roles they assign them in cognition, workflows, and decision-making.

The framework further introduces AIREOM, the AI as Relational Entity Optimization Model, as the practical optimization layer for Human-AI fit. For executives, product leaders, and AI strategy leaders, AIREOM expands the question of AI value beyond task automation. It asks what role users assign to the AI system in a given moment, what outcome they are trying to achieve, and what level of trust, delight, reliance, challenge, and business value the experience should support. In this view, Human-AI strategy becomes a market-expansion and customer-delight strategy, not merely a technical capability or user-experience feature.

The framework builds on the CASA (Computers Are Social Actors) paradigm developed by Clifford Nass, whose foundational insight — that people respond socially to computers — remains sound for the interaction patterns it was designed to explain. For the phenomena that increasingly characterize reliance on LLMs and agentic AI today — role assignment, differentiated trust across systems, and decision-consequential reliance — AIRE offers a broader and more complete account. A recurring strategic question threads through the paper: as AI systems proliferate across a user's workflow, will competition occur primarily between LLM models, or between the roles users distribute across those models?

This public disclosure intentionally summarizes the foundational theory, strategic significance, and business relevance of the framework while reserving detailed model architecture, scoring logic, measurement instruments, operationalization, and consulting applications for the full paper. The objective is to establish the public conceptual foundation of AIRE and AIREOM and to make the strategic category clear to C-suite, AI product, corporate strategy, and agentic AI leaders.

detail.abstract:
This article focuses on corporate law’s relentless “race for the bottom.” To establish that this situation is not solely one of company law, the article first highlights certain deficiencies in the enforcement of the federal securities laws. Thereafter, the article addresses state corporation law. First, the states’ “race for the bottom” from an historical perspective is succinctly addressed. Second, the article takes issue with the continued identification of corporate directors and officers as fiduciaries. A new and neutral term is suggested: corporate directors and officers are “discretionaries.” Third, the laxity that prevails under state company law with respect to director and officer liability standards is examined. Fourth, the article assesses the recent Texas legislation. The article concludes with several reflections on the importance of this subject and the possible detrimental impact of the undue laxity that prevails.

The prospective consequences of this inordinate diminution of director and officer duties are disconcerting. Unfortunately, it may be a matter of time before this country experiences major scandals that may be traced to the permissiveness that is authorized by several states. If and when this harmful eventuality occurs, the end result may be the further federalization of corporate governance. This federalization may encompass traditional aspects of state company law, including the setting forth of minimum standards of conduct in director and officer self-dealing transactions as well as other situations where the duty of loyalty arises.

title: Multi-Asset Scenario Stress Lab: Evidence-Constrained Scenario Analysis for Portfolio Stress Decision Support

detail.title: Multi-Asset Scenario Stress Lab: Evidence-Constrained Scenario Analysis for Portfolio Stress Decision Support

detail.abstract:
The Multi-Asset Scenario Stress Lab is an operational research system for scenario-based portfolio stress decision support. It generates 5,000 joint 20-trading-day return paths for eight liquid ETFs and evaluates whether more complex scenario models provide decision-relevant information beyond transparent conventional benchmarks.

The research design separates model development, validation, and primary out-of-sample (OOS) evaluation. Data from 2006–2014 are used for initial training, 2015–2018 for validation and model selection, and 2019–2025 for a single primary OOS evaluation without post-OOS tuning. The candidate set includes historical block resampling, EWMA-t, DCC-GARCH and hidden Markov model benchmarks, a conditional variational autoencoder, a conditional diffusion model, and a conditional Flow Matching model.

The primary OOS evidence did not establish predictive superiority for the modern generative models. B1, an exponentially weighted moving-average Student-t simulator, delivered the best overall performance among the conventional models, including the lowest mean 20-day Energy Score and standardized CRPS, lower overall calibration errors, and lower errors on the main dependence diagnostics. Flow F1 remained competitive and computationally efficient, but did not establish superiority over B1.

A subsequent five-use-case decision-value program examined whether the scenario distributions supported specific practical applications. Because this program reused the 2019–2025 interval already examined in the primary OOS evaluation, it is explicitly retrospective rather than a new independent OOS test. Four proposed uses did not meet their pre-specified qualification criteria: predictive downside signaling, a dynamic defensive overlay, tail-driver attribution, and a model-disagreement reliability warning. The only retained use was stress-archetype representation. Across 56 large-drawdown origins, B1 assigned a larger share of tail scenarios to the archetype that subsequently matched the realized stress pattern and produced representative cross-asset stress geometry closer to the realized outcome than historical block resampling. It also satisfied the pre-specified simulation-stability and leave-one-year-out robustness checks.

The resulting system is deliberately narrow. Scenario-family shares are frequencies within the generated scenario distribution, not calibrated real-world event probabilities. The system does not issue trading signals, automatic defensive allocations, optimized portfolio weights, or model-confidence indicators. Its contribution is therefore not a new generative model, but an evidence-constrained process for converting probabilistic scenario research into bounded and auditable portfolio stress decision support.

title: Does ChatGPT Understand Grammar, or Just Predict It? Reopening a Fifty-Year War Over Meaning in the Age of Large Language Models

detail.title: Does ChatGPT Understand Grammar, or Just Predict It? Reopening a Fifty-Year War Over Meaning in the Age of Large Language Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the developer of Learnable Theory, the framework applied in this paper to Miller's (2026) work on attentional omission. The paper's central claims are evaluated on their theoretical and predictive merits, and the author has no financial or personal relationship with Miller or with any organisation that could be perceived to have influenced the analysis presented here.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a theoretical paper. It did not involve human participants, animal subjects, or the collection of new empirical data; the driving case discussed throughout is a hypothetical example drawn from Miller (2026), not a conducted study. The three-arm simulator design and the physiological measures proposed in Section 7 as a methodological blueprint for future research have not been carried out and would require separate ethics review, including informed consent from participants, before being run.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The emergence of large language models has reopened a controversy theoretical linguistics never fully closed: whether grammar is an autonomous formal system, separate from meaning, or inseparable from it from the start. This paper traces that dispute from its origin in the break between Noam Chomsky and Ronald Langacker to its present form, the disagreement between Emily Bender and Alexander Koller, who argue that a system trained on form alone cannot acquire meaning, and Steven Piantadosi, who argues that contemporary language models already show functional evidence that they have. Neither position has won: a 2023 survey found the research community close to evenly split on whether these systems understand anything at all. The paper argues that a third position, developed independently by the philosopher Emma Borg and by Learnable Theory, reframes the dispute rather than resolving it in either direction. Grammar represents relations among three distinct levels of reality, the Real, the Actual, and the Empirical, and a system trained purely on text can plausibly master the representational patterns belonging to one of these levels without ever touching the other two. This accounts for why large language models are simultaneously fluent and structurally limited, and lets Chomsky and Langacker, and Bender and Piantadosi, both be right, about different things.

detail.abstract:
This research note examines the 2026 depreciation of the Indian rupee against the U.S. dollar despite India's strong external buffers and a positive India–U.S. 10-year yield differential. It analyses the interaction of oil prices, foreign portfolio flows, global dollar conditions, fiscal composition, RBI intervention and the emerging global AI investment cycle.

A central investment question is whether India's higher sovereign bond yield translates into superior returns for foreign investors once INR depreciation and duration risk are considered. Using the 18 August 2026 market levels, the note estimates a carry-only one-year FX break-even of approximately ₹97.62/$ for an Indian 10-year yield of 6.827% versus a U.S. 10-year yield of 4.708%.

The analysis also examines India's foreign-investor G-Sec policy reforms, including tax and market-access changes, and contrasts FY26 FPI equity outflows with continued debt inflows. It proposes AI-related capital allocation as a testable additional channel for explaining international portfolio reallocation, while explicitly avoiding a causal conclusion because the destination of Indian equity outflows is not directly observed.

The note concludes that the 2026 episode represents market pressure within a substantially stronger external balance sheet than in 1991, rather than a classical external-financing crisis. It identifies several empirical avenues for further research, including econometric analysis of oil, FPI flows, RBI intervention and AI-related investment.

title: Real Options for Systemic Resilience and Viability: Experimental Analysis of Process Flexibility Design
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Real Estate and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - School of Engineering

detail.title: Real Options for Systemic Resilience and Viability: Experimental Analysis of Process Flexibility Design

publicationDetails.detailsText: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper No. 2026/008
publicationDetails.journalName: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Pandemics, tariffs, product launches, and competitive pressures exemplify large-scale systemic changes (or shocks) that reshape product portfolios and threaten the long-term viability of manufacturing systems. We focus on proactive adaptability and viability under such shocks by developing a two-stage, multi-period stochastic mixed integer linear program (SMILP) that jointly optimizes investments in resources (plants) and process flexibility (plant-product capabilities). Investment timing is embedded in a net present value (NPV) framework inspired by real-options thinking, so capacity and flexibility can be staged over multiple periods rather than committed upfront. Systemic change is modeled through multi-period demand uncertainty with stable, increasing, and decreasing demand paths, while stochastic capacity, single-point disruptions, and finite resource lifetimes are also incorporated. We benchmark the proposed design against three established alternatives: a start-period design that invests all resources and flexibility upfront, a long-chain design, and a simple decision-rule heuristic. Under stable demand paths, stochastic capacity, and single-point disruptions, the multi-period and start-period designs perform nearly identically to the long-chain benchmark and converge to comparable sparse structures, confirming that long-chain or start-period designs are essentially sufficient in such environments. Under systemic change, however, especially when portfolios contain high-margin growth products, the multi-period design yields substantial improvements in expected NPV by deferring and targeting investments. Specifically, the multi-period approach generates expected NPV gains of approximately 4%-7% relative to the start-period design and up to 12% relative to the long-chain design in stylized experiments, alongside a $7.8M improvement in the industrial case study. The results provide an adaptation-based framework that helps managers determine when classical long-chain or start-period flexibility designs are sufficient and when a multi-period design is necessary to sustain long-term viability in the face of systemic changes.

detail.title: Organizational Change and Design: Preaching What they Practiced for 50 years
detail.abstract: This essay celebrates the golden anniversary of Bob Hinings and Royston Greenwood's collaboration by examining both what they theorized and how they worked. Their configurational framework-design archetypes, interpretive schemes, and organizational tracks-resolved a longstanding impasse between structural contingency theory and early institutionalism, linking micro-level sensemaking to fieldlevel transformation. Yet rereading their work and examining their working practices revealed something I had not seen despite a forty-year personal and intellectual relationship with them: their careers instantiated their theory. Their co-located research teams enacted interpretive communities; their Alberta workshops operated as fieldconfiguring events; their mentoring institutionalized an invisible college carrying their norms and practices to new generations. Hinings and Greenwood did not merely study organizational change and design-they designed, and changed, the field itself.

detail.abstract: The quantitative side of investing is well studied, with many recognizable phrases such as herding behavior and fear of missing out bias. Yet, few existing experiments look towards the qualitative side, digging into the why behind investing decisions. This paper puts a dent in that, describing that team-based investing is a process in which sequential and frequently subconscious checkpoints are reached before a buy or sell decision is made. Two factors make this particularly unique, (1) a period of heightened market volatility and (2) the study group consisting of college students. Under these conditions, the conclusions reached point towards teams with consistent investing principles and frequent communication resulting in higher returns.

detail.abstract: Authorized and unauthorized production trajectories can generate the same acceptable output. When they do, final-output control cannot reveal whether delegated execution remained organizationally authorized. Agentic artificial intelligence makes this problem salient by combining consequential execution discretion with comparatively low responsiveness to actor-specific future consequences within the focal organizational relationship. We develop a contingency theory that separates delegated execution discretion from localized payoff responsiveness. Under incomplete mandates, capable artificial executors can systematically favor locally task-improving paths that violate authorization conditions absent from the operative decision state, producing mandate drift without preference divergence. Three propositions predict when trajectory-level obligations make final outputs non-diagnostic, why low payoff responsiveness both buffers execution from misaligned local incentives and forfeits the benefits of aligned ones, and why trajectory access becomes increasingly complementary with mandate knowledge and interpretive competence as output diagnosticity declines. The theory extends organizational delegation by identifying a high-discretion, low-payoff-responsive configuration in which incentive alignment loses leverage while authorization-path governance becomes consequential.

detail.abstract: Attribution in a transcript is harder than transcription. A question may supply the disputed premise, restrict the reply, fix the sequence, and influence how uncertainty is heard. The resulting answer can be verbally exact while adding little independent support. This article develops an evidence-bounded account of questioning. The weight assigned to an answer should follow its provenance: what the respondent contributed, what the examiner supplied, which records were available, and whether correction remained practicable. Studies of institutional talk, pragmatics, eyewitness memory and investigative interviewing are used at the level of their actual designs. The article therefore places specimen questions beside the inferences later drawn from them, including compound formulations and the wording manipulations used by Loftus and Palmer and by Loftus and Zanni. It separates personal recollection from an authorised organisational position. Disclosure sequence is treated as part of the evidence. The proposed method preserves strong challenge while requiring the report to expose the path from question to finding.

title: Beyond the Textbook Consensus: Capital Budgeting Technique Choice (NPV, IRR, Payback) Across Institutional Regimes — A Comparative Synthesis and Atlas

detail.title: Beyond the Textbook Consensus: Capital Budgeting Technique Choice (NPV, IRR, Payback) Across Institutional Regimes — A Comparative Synthesis and Atlas

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationship with any person or organization that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual-synthetic literature synthesis based entirely on previously published sources; no human participants, patients, or original primary data were involved.

detail.abstract: Corporate finance textbooks converge on a single normative answer to the capital budgeting problem: firms should rank and accept projects using Net Present Value (NPV), because NPV alone correctly aggregates the time value of money and the magnitude of value created. Five decades of field surveys, beginning with Graham and Harvey's (2001) landmark study of U.S. Chief Financial Officers, show a persistently different empirical picture. Internal Rate of Return (IRR) and, in many countries, the simple Payback Period rule remain co-dominant or outright dominant decision criteria. This monograph does not run a new primary survey. Instead, it performs the synthesis that the dispersed country-level literature has not yet produced: it collects roughly thirty published field studies spanning North America, Western and Central-Eastern Europe, East Asia, South Asia, Oceania, Southern Africa and Latin America, organizes them into a common comparative skeleton, and asks a single organizing question-for which countries, and under which institutional conditions, was IRR, NPV, or Payback the more relevant criterion in practice? Building on this synthesis, the book proposes an original secondary artifact, the Institutional Capital Budgeting Index (ICBI), which scores each covered country-study on its distance from the textbook NPV consensus as a function of four recurring institutional correlates identified across the literature: capital market depth, legal origin and investor protection, average CFO financial education, and typical firm size/ownership concentration in the sampled population. The exercise is explicitly conceptual-synthetic: the ICBI is a transparent recombination of already-published percentages, not a new empirical estimate, and every score is traceable to a cited source. The clearest finding of the synthesis is not about any single country-it is about the map itself: capital budgeting technique choice has been surveyed intensively in the United States, Western Europe, Japan, Australia and, more recently, Central-Eastern Europe and parts of Asia, while Latin America has exactly one region-wide survey (Maquieira, Preve and Sarria-Allende, 2012, covering seven countries but explicitly excluding Brazil) plus a handful of single-country Brazilian studies, and large parts of Sub-Saharan Africa and the Middle East remain essentially unsurveyed. The book closes by arguing that this asymmetry, not any single technique-choice finding, is the most policy-relevant gap in the literature, and sets out a concrete research agenda for closing it. Use of Artificial Intelligence: this manuscript was produced with the assistance of a large language model (Claude, Anthropic) for literature synthesis support, drafting, and editorial structuring, under the direct supervision, verification, and final authorship responsibility of the named author. All cited findings were checked against the original published sources listed in the References section before inclusion. No primary data was collected, simulated, or fabricated for this work; the Institutional Capital Budgeting Index presented in Part III is explicitly and transparently a secondary recombination of previously published percentages, not new empirical evidence.

detail.abstract: The consideration of this article is that it is pivotal for economic policy to have a framework that enables first to understand the determinants of growth and their respective weights, and then to examine prospectively the isolated (i.e., all other variables being equal) or aggregate impact of economic policy on potential growth. We have improved the precision of this framework by distinguishing between global, technological and human progress, by considering intermediate consumption (IC), and by dividing French economy into three productive sectors (including the ICT sector). We calibrated the model using a newly constructed dataset researchers may find useful. The results inform that, given its economic characteristics, France's potential growth is stagnant (0,11 %) and essentially (around 2/3) intensive explained by global progress and ICT-sector specific advances. The extensive part is due to capital deepening. Assessing the impact on potential growth of a number of variables that are central to economic policy, we obtain that TFP, whose contribution to potential growth was nil over the period studied, has the highest growth multiplier coefficient (slightly over 1). Within the typology of progress, the one passing through IC has the highest impact on growth (coefficient of 0.2).

title: The Hard Law-Soft Law Nexus: Autonomous Vehicles as a Case The Hard Law-Soft Law Nexus: Autonomous Vehicles as a Case Study Study
affiliations: Arizona State University - College of Law, Arizona State University and Arizona State University

detail.title: The Hard Law-Soft Law Nexus: Autonomous Vehicles as a Case The Hard Law-Soft Law Nexus: Autonomous Vehicles as a Case Study Study
detail.abstract: The technology governance debate often focuses on the dichotomy of hard law versus soft law as competing models. Both hard law and soft law have their strengths and weaknesses. But framing soft law versus hard law as a dichotomous choice is often unrealistic—every technology will be governed by a mix of hard law and soft law. So, the more realistic questions are where hard law works best and where soft law succeeds, and how these two types of governance interact and integrate. After reviewing the strengths and weaknesses of hard law and soft law, this Article identifies six different hybrid models integrating hard law and soft law. The Article then considers hybrid hard law/soft law models in the context of autonomous vehicles (AVs) as a case study. After reviewing the challenges and stunted progress of AV regulation, the analysis focuses on two recent rulemakings in which the first Trump and then Biden administrations proposed frameworks for AV regulation in the waning days of their respective administrations. Analysis of the comments submitted by the broad range of AV stakeholders shows a sharply divided community, with about half of the stakeholders adamantly supporting a hard law approach, and another half equally favoring a soft law approach. However, there was substantial support for hybrid hard law/soft law models, with all six models identified earlier in the article and two new models receiving support. Based on this analysis, the Article suggests that a hybrid hard law/soft law approach is the most promising direction for AV governance.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to explore how sports businesses can be reimagined in the digital era by identifying key transformative indicators shaped by virtualization. Methodology: The research is mixed-methods (qualitative and quantitative). The statistical population of the qualitative section included all IT specialists in the sports industry and university professors with expertise in sports management and digitalization from executive and academic fields. Purposive sampling was used to select the research sample. The sample size continued until theoretical saturation (15 people) was reached. In the initial stage, the data of this research were collected through semi-structured interviews with the selected samples. To ensure validity, various methods, such as tracking data over time (audit tracking) and consolidating findings through repeated assessments of data and patterns, were used. After the coding processes and identification of main themes and indicators, a questionnaire was developed to validate the extracted components. For qualitative data, content analysis was used, and in the quantitative phase, second-order confirmatory factor analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25 and Smart PLS version 3.

detail.abstract: On 13 February 2025, Retraction Watch announced the Elisabeth Bik Science Integrity Fund under the fiscal sponsorship of its parent nonprofit, The Center for Scientific Integrity (CSI). The Fund was launched with the proceeds of Bik's 2024 Einstein Foundation Individual Award and was described as a source of financial resources for Bik, other scientific sleuths and collaborators, as well as training, grants, awards, education and outreach. The announcement invited tax-deductible donations and stated that Bik would have full direction over the Fund's resources. This article examines what that formulation discloses and, more importantly, what it leaves unanswered. The current public Fund page does not identify the fiscal-sponsorship model, CSI's reserved approval authority, an administrative fee, an independent selection committee, eligibility or scoring rules, conflicts and recusal procedures, grant recipients, compensation paid to Bik or associated entities, donor-influence restrictions, recipient disclosure duties, an editorial firewall, a complaints process, or project-level annual accounts. Those omissions are material because the programme can finance people whose allegations may affect researchers, journals and institutions, while CSI also operates Retraction Watch, its database and related sleuthing initiatives. Fiscal sponsorship is not a decorative route to tax deductibility: recognised nonprofit guidance requires the sponsor to retain control and discretion over charitable funds, while transparent governance requires clear expenditure authority, conflicts management, truthful solicitation and financial reporting. The announcement's promise of personal direction is therefore either imprecise or incomplete unless it is expressly subordinated to CSI's ultimate fiduciary authority and independent review. No reviewed source shows a pay-per-retraction bounty, an unlawful pass-through, donor-directed targeting, improper self-payment, or a particular conflicted decision. The defensible conclusion is narrower but still severe: the public governance offered for a consequential, named, donor-funded investigative programme is inadequate to the transparency standard it invokes. The Fund should publish a charter, independent grant and compensation controls, donor and recipient conflict rules, activity-level funding disclosures, outcome-neutral performance measures, a correction and appeal process, and annual project accounts before it seeks further public trust.

title: Procurement Strategies Under Operational and Policy Disruptions: The Role of Sourcing Agents
affiliations: , Fudan University - School of Management, Harbin Institute of Technology and Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Department of Logistics and Maritime Studies

detail.title: Procurement Strategies Under Operational and Policy Disruptions: The Role of Sourcing Agents
detail.abstract: Supply disruptions caused by operational failures and policy shocks are prevalent in global manufacturing. However, the optimal procurement decisions and the strategic value of sourcing agents under such dual risks have not been fully understood. In this paper, we investigate a manufacturer's optimal procurement and contract design decisions under both operational and policy disruption risks. Specifically, we study a three-tier supply chain model in which a manufacturer designs contracts to incentivize Tier 1 suppliers, who then allocate orders among Tier 2 suppliers and an external channel operated by a sourcing agent. We characterize the optimal supply chain structures and the corresponding contract parameters. We show that, although disruption risks are mostly perceived as harmful, a higher disruption probability may reduce the wholesale price required to induce a Tier 1 supplier to adopt a mitigation action. The introduction of the agent channel broadens this positive contractual effect. Under the corresponding agent-based structures, worsening operational or policy disruptions can strengthen the Tier 1 supplier's incentive to use guaranteed external capacity, allowing the manufacturer to induce the same sourcing decision at a lower wholesale price. This reduction in the incentive payment can exceed the additional risk burden and increase the manufacturer's profit. We further show that agent-channel adoption depends on the interplay between disruption risks and procurement costs. A high-cost agent serves mainly as a conditional backup option, whereas access to a cost-competitive agent can either strictly increase or strictly decrease the manufacturer's optimal profit. Consequently, manufacturers should look beyond the physical mitigation value of sourcing agents. The agent channel not only provides capacity outside the affected upstream network but also changes Tier 1 sourcing incentives and the allocation of profit within the supply chain.

detail.abstract: Introduction. United States e-cigarette policy is judged by prevalence and by the number of authorized products. Neither measure whether authorization reaches the products adolescents use. We estimated regulatory reach, the share of youth users whose usual product is lawfully marketed. Methods. The 2024 (n = 29,861) and 2025 (n = 23,630) National Youth Tobacco Survey publicuse files were analyzed with design-based variance estimation. Usual brand was classified against Food and Drug Administration marketing orders as authorized, marketed under a judicial stay, or unauthorized; reach also required reported flavors to match a lawful variant. Underreported theft and unknown brand were addressed by Monte Carlo bias analysis. Results. In 2025, 5.2% (95% CI 4.7 to 5.9) of students currently used e-cigarettes. Among users with brand data (n = 1,337), Geek Bar was the usual brand of 48.3% and an authorized brand of 5.1% (3.3 to 7.9). Only 2.0% (1.1 to 3.7) used a lawfully marketed product in a lawful flavor, all Vuse menthol pods sold under a court stay; none used a marketing-granted-order product in an authorized flavor. Every youth who usually used JUUL reported a flavor for which JUUL holds no marketing order. In 2024 the figures were 4.0% and 1.6%. Bias-corrected reach was 2.8% (1.5 to 4.7). In England, 48.4% of young vapers used Elf Bar, a notified product under the 20 mg/mL cap. Conclusions. Lawfully marketed products account for about one in fifty United States youth ecigarette users, unchanged as prevalence fell. Authorization denial governs what is sold, not what adolescents use. Implications. This is the first user-level estimate of the share of United States youth e-cigarette use covered by federal authorization. It is near zero under a strict reading and about 2% counting court-stayed products, and it did not rise while youth prevalence fell. The comparison with England, where the same manufacturers sell notified products at lawful nicotine concentrations, shows that the discriminating policy variable is whether a standard reaches the product, not whether flavors are permitted. The indicator, the derivation of usual brand from existing NYTS items, and the bias-analysis code are provided for routine use. Summary of research (25 words). Federal authorization reaches about 2% of United States adolescents who vape, near zero under a strict reading, and did not rise as prevalence fell.

title: Hamas-Fatah Reconciliation and the Prospects for Palestinian-Israeli Peace
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Hamas-Fatah Reconciliation and the Prospects for Palestinian-Israeli Peace

contentType.other: HAMAS-FATAH RECONCILIATION AND THE PROSPECTS FOR PALESTINIAN-ISRAELI PEACE (a thesis)

detail.abstract:
This thesis investigates the political and ideological conflict between Hamas and Fatah following Hamas's military takeover of the Gaza Strip in June 2007, situating intra-Palestinian division within the broader frameworks of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and the dynamics between Islamism and the West. It examines the historical evolution of both organizations—tracing Fatah’s transition from armed struggle toward national-secularism, international diplomacy, and the two-state framework, alongside Hamas’s emergence as an Islamist resistance movement offering a counter-hegemonic alternative to the Oslo Peace Process.


The study argues that the persistent division between Hamas and Fatah, as well as the broader stalemate in Palestinian-Israeli negotiations, is fundamentally driven by four competing and conflicting visions of peace: a secular two-state solution, a secular bi-national one-state solution, a Jewish radical one-state vision, and an Islamic one-state framework. By analyzing the structural limitations of the Oslo-Roadmap process, platform terms, and the international boycott of the elected Hamas government, the thesis demonstrates how absolute paradigms of justice and divine mandate create an enduring obstacle to conflict transformation.


Drawing on peace studies theoretical frameworks—including Lynne Belaief's concept of "tragic justice" and Wolfgang Dietrich and Wolfgang Sützl's "many peaces"—the author concludes that a sustainable, living peace requires moving away from unachievable zero-sum absolutes. It asserts that intra-Palestinian reconciliation and regional stability ultimately depend on accepting core political and historical realities: acknowledging the Israeli national identity alongside the imperative of a fully sovereign Palestinian state, with the pragmatic two-state compromise remaining the most viable mechanism for immediate conflict transformation.

detail.title: Contract Incompleteness, Behavioral Boundaries, and the Allocation of Income Rights

detail.abstract: This paper studies how marginal income rights and behavioral restrictions are jointly designed in incomplete contractual relationships when parties make non-contractible investments and retain residual discretion over subsequent resource use. Each contractual instrument affects surplus through two channels: it changes the ex post use of existing productive capacity and the ex ante incentives to create that capacity. Income rights and behavioral restrictions are therefore structurally substitutable in governing residual behavior, so constraints on one contractual margin induce endogenous rebalancing along the others. The framework also endogenizes organizational regimes. Continuous changes in governance difficulty, investment dependence, and cross-firm appropriability alter the relative values of interior sharing and concentrated income-rights boundaries, potentially generating discrete institutional transitions. The analysis provides a unified interpretation of contractual adjustment and organizational change, with applications to platform regulation, shopping malls, and share tenancy.

title: Staying Agile in the Saddle: CEO Tenure, TMT Characteristics, and Organizational Ambidexterity
affiliations: , University of St. Gallen and Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Staying Agile in the Saddle: CEO Tenure, TMT Characteristics, and Organizational Ambidexterity
detail.abstract: Upper echelons theory describes long-tenured CEOs as a liability for their organizations. Drawing on ambidexterity theory, we argue that CEOs can stay 'agile in the saddle' by developing and refreshing their organization's ability to simultaneously explore and exploit. Our core conceptual idea is that the appropriate timing of TMT changes in relation to the CEO's tenure promotes ambidexterity. While TMT change is negatively related to ambidexterity in the early CEO tenure seasons, it has a positive relationship to ambidexterity in the advanced CEO tenure seasons. We further show that different types of TMT diversity play a complementary role for enabling ambidexterity in the early and advanced CEO tenure stages. We test and find support for our propositions using a longitudinal sample of 98 leading Financial Service companies. We contribute to the upper echelons theory by developing an alternative perspective to the CEO lifecycle that reveals the benefits of long-tenured CEOs, suggests decoupling of CEO and TMT changes, and promotes complementary CEO-TMT configurations. Furthermore, we inform ambidexterity theory by developing a process perspective of how leadership dynamics enable and sustain an organization's dual attention to exploration and exploitation.

title: Autonomous AI Agents and Legal Personality: Agency, Attribution, and the Limits of Artificial Intelligence Liability

detail.title: Autonomous AI Agents and Legal Personality: Agency, Attribution, and the Limits of Artificial Intelligence Liability
detail.abstract: This article examines a doctrinal confusion that has shaped a decade of legal scholarship on artificial intelligence: the conflation of the question "should an autonomous AI system hold legal personality" with the distinct question "to whom should an autonomous AI system's acts be attributed." Courts and legislatures confronting autonomous AI agents have, almost without exception, answered the first question in the negative — the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and the United Kingdom Supreme Court both held that an artificial intelligence system cannot be a patent inventor because inventorship requires a natural person — while leaving the second question to be resolved, unevenly and often accidentally, through pre-existing doctrines of agency, vicarious liability, and product liability that were not built for systems capable of independent linguistic negotiation with third parties. Drawing on comparative material from the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, Canada, and Brazil, this article argues that legal personality has functioned as a distraction from the harder and more tractable question of attribution architecture. It develops the concept of an "attribution vacuum": a structural gap that opens when an AI system's functional autonomy exceeds the scope of authority any human or corporate principal actually manifested, so that neither classical agency law nor product liability law can identify a clean bearer of responsibility without doctrinal strain. Using the 2024 Canadian small-claims decision in a chatbot-misrepresentation dispute, the European Union's now-withdrawn AI Liability Directive, and the 2024 revision of the EU Product Liability Directive as evidentiary anchors, the article proposes the Delegated Autonomy Attribution Standard (DAAS), a three-tier framework that classifies AI-mediated conduct by the degree of principal displacement it exhibits and assigns the applicable liability doctrine accordingly, without requiring any new legal subject. The article concludes that attribution, not personality, is the doctrinally load-bearing concept, and that regulatory energy currently spent debating electronic personhood would be better directed at closing the attribution vacuum within existing private law categories.

title: From Community-Based Initiative to National Public Policy: An Analysis of the Cisternas Programme in Brazil

detail.title: From Community-Based Initiative to National Public Policy: An Analysis of the Cisternas Programme in Brazil
detail.abstract: This paper analyses the implementation of the Cisternas Programme in Brazil, examining its transition from a community-based initiative to a national public policy. Using the 3R framework (resources, relationships, and rules of the game) and the Levels and Scales approach, the study draws on qualitative document analysis to explore how governance arrangements shaped programme delivery and expansion. The findings show that implementation relied on a hybrid model combining federal coordination with decentralised execution through civil society organisations and community participation. This structure enabled the incorporation of local knowledge and contextspecific solutions, supporting delivery across diverse territories. The programme's exclusive dependence on federal funding, however, created a structural vulnerability to political and fiscal cycles. The analysis highlights the importance of aligning governance structures with resource allocation mechanisms, offering insights relevant to climate adaptation policies that seek to integrate social development and poverty alleviation.

keywords: and the Governance Deficit in Professionalised Scientific Sleuthing

detail.abstract: A May 2019 Retraction Watch headline presented Elisabeth Bik as finding problematic images ‘for free’, while the item highlighted her statement: ‘We need this to be a career that people can make money and use their talents in’. The full profile makes clear that Bik was described as unpaid at that time and was advocating paid integrity positions at journals, universities and research institutes. The two statements are therefore not a literal contradiction, and the quotation does not establish that personal profit was Bik’s sole motive. It does, however, mark an explicit programme to professionalise an activity capable of damaging careers and altering the scholarly record. By August 2026, public disclosures described paid but usually confidential consultancy for publishers and institutions, honoraria, a former committee stipend, Patreon income, and a fund able to provide resources to Bik and others. This article argues that the promotional language of volunteerism has not been matched by a comparably visible framework for financial disclosure, case-level recusal, client-conflict checking, independent fund governance, correction, appeal and audit. Paid criticism is not necessarily false; unpaid criticism is not necessarily independent. In either case, observations should remain leads for independent examination, not substitutes for adjudication.

title: Identifying Barriers to Digital Transformation in Kenya's IT Firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Identifying Barriers to Digital Transformation in Kenya's IT Firms
detail.abstract: Digital transformation has become a key strategic priority for organizations seeking to remain competitive in an increasingly technology-driven economy. Despite its importance, digital transformation often falters because of internal organizational challenges rather than technological limitations. Although Kenya is widely recognized as a leader in Africa's digital economy and is often described as the continent's "Silicon Savannah," its IT firms continue to experience internal barriers that hinder transformation. This study examined organizational barriers to digital transformation in Kenya's IT firms using Vial's (2019) theoretical framework. A sequential, two-stage mixed-methods design was employed. First, a scoping review conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR assessed 195 full-text articles and included 60 studies in the final synthesis. The review identified six broad barrier categories, which informed a survey of 201 IT professionals and semi-structured interviews with three key informants in the second stage. Qualitative data were analyzed using the Gioia methodology. Resource constraints received the highest reported severity rating (33.9%), followed by cultural resistance (33.1%), skills gaps (29.9%), insufficient strategic clarity (28.5%), weak leadership commitment (25.0%), and organizational structure barriers (21.1%). Operations was the business dimension most consistently affected. The qualitative analysis also identified three barriers that were particularly salient in the Kenyan context: post-training talent drain, dependence on externally developed software that did not always align with local needs, and informal recruitment practices that could overlook digitally skilled candidates. The findings indicate that effective digital transformation in Kenya's IT firms requires an integrated response involving leadership, operational change, skills development and retention, locally relevant technological solutions, and supportive policy measures.

detail.abstract: This study examines how organizational hierarchy and policy salience condition the symbolic effects of gender representation, drawing on the mirror-image and institutionalsymbol perspectives to explain how representation shapes citizen evaluations. Using a preregistered 3 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, we find evidence that both mechanisms operate, highlighting the contextual complexity of symbolic representation. Female representation across hierarchical levels generally improves perceived performance, trust, and procedural justice across citizen genders, although female managerial representation generates stronger positive responses among women. Policy salience also conditions these effects, though contrary to expectations. Female representation does not gain additional benefit in a female-salient domain; rather, it draws less favorable evaluations when paired with a male-salient context, suggesting a penalty for gender-policy mismatch rather than a bonus for gender-policy fit. By clarifying how and when representation produces symbolic effects, this study refines symbolic representation theory and moves beyond conventional debates over its binary effectiveness.

title: Nonlinear Trade-Offs in Genai Application Pricing: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of API and Psychological Costs
affiliations: , Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xidian University and Xidian University

detail.title: Nonlinear Trade-Offs in Genai Application Pricing: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of API and Psychological Costs
detail.abstract: In the rapidly evolving generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) ecosystem, downstream application providers face persistent challenges in designing optimal pricing strategies. These challenges arise from dual cost pressures: application programming interface (API) costs imposed by upstream model platforms and psychological frictions experienced by end consumers. This study develops a game-theoretic model to analyze application providers' strategic choice between subscriptionbased and usage-based pricing under both monopolistic and duopolistic market structures. The analysis reveals that the optimal strategies are shaped by a nonlinear interplay among psychological costs, model API costs, and consumer valuation. Under low psychological-cost conditions, API costs exert an inverted U-shaped effect on competing providers' profits. By contrast, under high API-cost regimes, subscription-based and usage-based models exhibit asymmetric sensitivities to psychological costs: profits under usage-based pricing decline with rising psychological costs, whereas subscription-based profits stabilise. Fthermore, elevated API and psychological costs attenuate competitive intensity, driving duopolistic equilibria toward monopoly-like outcomes. These findings remain robust after incorporating a broad set of realistic market frictions. The results provide actionable insights for GenAI application providers balancing cost pass-through, user engagement, and competitive positioning in pricing decisions.
