detail.abstract: Sudan's recurring cycles of internal fragmentation are conventionally analyzed as products of domestic bargaining failure. We argue instead that the composition and timing of Sudanese factional realignment-from the Assyrian expulsion of the 25th Dynasty (671-656 BCE) through the Turco-Egyptian and Anglo-Egyptian periods to the 2023-present war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF)-has consistently tracked the investment decisions of competing external sponsors rather than internal grievance alone. We adapt a compartmental replicator-mutator framework [1,2], introduce a patron-capture forcing term discounted by Sudan's economic leverage, derive a sponsor-divergence index [3,4], and formalize a strategic-retreat threshold using Napata-to-Meroe as calibration anchor [5]. The central result is a race condition: whether the July-August 2026 wave of RSF defections consolidates depends on whether Lambda_k rises faster than sponsor replenishment B_k recovers. Four falsifiable predictions are stated for ex post testing against ACLED, remittance, and export-revenue data [6].

title: Do Data Centers Raise your Electricity Bill? Evidence from U.S. States
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: Do Data Centers Raise your Electricity Bill? Evidence from U.S. States
detail.abstract: Data-center investment has become one of the largest capital-expenditure cycles in financial markets, with U.S. hyperscalers expected to deploy roughly $700 billion in 2026. This investment boom has raised concerns that large computing loads impose external costs on households through higher electricity prices. Using a 50-state panel for 2021-2024, we find no statistically significant evidence that data-center presence, installed capacity, or capacity expansion predicts residential electricity-price inflation across extensive-margin, intensive-margin, fixed-effects, and timing specifications. We propose an energyinternalization mechanism: hyperscalers can partially internalize incremental electricity demand through contracted or dedicated generation, including solar and wind energy. Consequently, gross datacenter electricity consumption need not translate one-for-one into net pressure on residential electricity supply. The findings suggest that the extraordinary AI capital-investment cycle has not, thus far, produced a detectable residential electricity-price externality.

title: Penalizing Passivity: Enforcement and the Reallocation of Scoring in IJF Judo

detail.title: Penalizing Passivity: Enforcement and the Reallocation of Scoring in IJF Judo
detail.abstract: Does the referee's call produce the dynamism it is meant to? The International Judo Federation justifies the sport's most frequent penalty-the shido for passivity-as a device for producing action. We test that claim with the federation's own event tagged records of 40,459 elite contests. Within-fight event studies face a mechanical trap general to sports that end at the studied outcome: the match's terminal, outcome-containing bin follows any event placed inside the match, so post-event coefficients inflate by construction. Bracketing the artifact with two permutation nulls, the aggregate claim fails: total scoring after a passivity call is bounded within two percentage points of its mechanical baseline, sign unidentified. What survives every null, rule era, and subsample is a category contrast: the passivity penalty, which uniquely obliges visible attack, raises the penalized athlete's scoring hazard by 2.5 percentage points relative to an identically priced gripping penalty that carries no mandate-entirely at the waza-ari grade, trebling at the second shido, and among men only. Enforcement redirects action; it is not shown to produce it.

title: Dark Matter in Platform Antitrust: Severing Markets after American Express

detail.title: Dark Matter in Platform Antitrust: Severing Markets after American Express
detail.abstract: This Note will propose a three-element market severance test for antitrust cases involving digital platforms that extract non-salient value-attention, behavioral data, and privacy-from users. Drawing an analogy to dark matter in astrophysics, the Note will identify a category of platform extraction that current antitrust frameworks cannot detect: value that users neither perceive nor optimize around, rendering the cross-side competitive discipline that Ohio v. American Express Co. assumes inoperative. The proposed test will apply when a platform (1) provides independent core services to each side rather than facilitating joint transactions, (2) extracts substantial non-salient value from users, and (3) faces no effective cross-side elasticity because user-side degradation amplifies rather than reduces advertiser-side demand. When all three elements are satisfied, courts will define separate markets for each platform side. The Note will demonstrate the test's application to social media networks, search engines, and mobile app ecosystems, and will defend it against administrability, over-deterrence, and stare decisis objections through error-cost analysis.

title: The Border That Never Rests

detail.title: The Border That Never Rests

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationship with any other person or organization that has or could be perceived to have influenced this study, beyond his role as Founder and Executive Chairman of Latino Institute for Security Efficiency (LISE), the organization under whose working paper series this document is published.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a policy and security-analysis working paper based on publicly available news reporting, government designations, and humanitarian-organization reports. It does not involve human subjects, patients, or the collection of primary data requiring ethics approval or participant consent.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted and funded internally by Latino Institute for Security Efficiency (LISE).

detail.abstract: Between June and August 2026, three processes converged on the same geography that had previously advanced on separate tracks. In Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella won the presidency on June 22, formally broke with his predecessor's "Total Peace" doctrine, and, following his inauguration on August 7, deployed a 90-day military offensive over the Catatumbo region explicitly directed at "securing the frontier zone with Venezuela, to restrict ELN and FARC dissident leaders who operate from neighboring territory." In Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez's transitional government completed, on August 15, a near-total reconfiguration of the territorial military command in the states bordering Colombia, seven months after the capture of Nicolás Maduro on January 3. And on August 24, De la Espriella himself announced a migration policy of enforcement operations and deportations that, according to academic evidence cited in this document, risks producing the opposite of its stated effect. This working paper examines how these three processes interact over the same civilian population, quantifies the human cost documented in the border zone during 2025 and 2026, assesses the structural position of the ELN and FARC dissidents on both sides of the border, examines the framework of United States designations and security cooperation applicable to the region, and offers a forward-looking analysis of three scenarios through 2027, together with concrete mitigation measures.

title: Trials-adjusted Out-of-Sample Gating for LLM-proposed Trading Strategies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Trials-adjusted Out-of-Sample Gating for LLM-proposed Trading Strategies
detail.abstract: A language model can propose trading strategies faster than a human can read them. That capability is close to worthless on its own, because the binding constraint in systematic trading was never idea generation; it is not being fooled by ideas that only worked in the past. A strategy selected as the best of many candidates carries selection bias: its in-sample performance is inflated by luck in proportion to how many candidates were tried, and that inflation is invisible to the naive backtest that produced it. This paper describes and evaluates a validation gate built to be un-foolable by construction, and reports what happens when it is pointed at real markets. The system, ÀYÒ, separates a nondeterministic proposer (an LLM that authors strategies as typed, content-hashed data artifacts, never as executable code) from a deterministic verifier that trades only the frozen artifact. The verifier enforces three defenses against backtest overfitting: strict out-of-sample evaluation via a walk-forward split, a trials-adjusted acceptance bar whose required out-of-sample Sharpe rises with the number of candidates tested, and robustness sweeps across rolling windows and parameter settings. We run all three on 2-4 years of real U.S. equity data (Alpaca daily bars, 32-83 symbols, ending 2026-07-17) and report every number the gate produced. A single rule-based strategy selected for its insample Sharpe of 3.07 collapsed to an out-of-sample Sharpe of-4.90 and was rejected. A cross-sectional momentum book that appeared to beat buy-and-hold out-of-sample by a Sharpe edge of +0.13 in one configuration was exposed by the robustness sweep as a fluke: it beat the benchmark in only 2 of 5 rolling windows and in 0 of 12 parameter settings. Under honest validation, nothing survived-which is the expected and correct result on efficient large-cap markets, and precisely the outcome the gate exists to enforce. We argue that the contribution is not an alpha but a methodology: a reproducible gate that reliably refuses to deploy mirages, and that generalizes to any setting where a nondeterministic proposer must be held to a deterministic guarantee. We are explicit throughout about which claims the evidence supports and which remain open.

title: Short-Term Gains, Long-Term Losses: The Microeconomic Consequences of Child Labor

detail.title: Short-Term Gains, Long-Term Losses: The Microeconomic Consequences of Child Labor
detail.abstract: This study examines the microeconomic dynamics among child poverty, child labor, and occupational accidents through a theoretical model. In the existing literature, child labor is predominantly analyzed in relation to poverty and education, while the longterm effects on health capital have generally remained secondary. By incorporating the health dimension into the analysis, this article offers an original contribution. Within a two-period model, households choose between child labor and education in order to meet short-term consumption needs, and the analysis shows that these choices lead to long-term welfare losses through both human capital and health capital channels. The findings indicate that income transfers reduce child labor in the short run; investments in education play a lasting role in breaking the intergenerational cycle of poverty; and occupational health and safety measures help mitigate adverse outcomes. The study emphasizes that the fight against child labor requires multidimensional strategies on the part of policymakers * Corresponding author.

title: The Valuation of Control Attached to Shares
affiliations: and Berenschot Business Management

detail.title: The Valuation of Control Attached to Shares
detail.abstract:
In legal proceedings concerning the valuation of shares, the question regularly arises as to whether the value of control attached to those shares can be considered separately and, if so, how. In this article, the authors address these questions and propose a concrete method for determining the value of control. This method combines insights from classical valuation theory with established concepts from game theory. 

The value of control for a (prospective) shareholder depends on three variables: (i) the shareholder value of the company assuming a stand-alone going concern situation; (ii) the shareholder value of the company assuming it is optimally managed; and (iii) the extent to which the shareholder has actual control through the exercise of their voting rights. 

Within game theory, extensive research has been conducted into how much influence a particular actor with a certain number of voting rights can have on the outcome of a vote, given the distribution of the other voting rights. One of the best-known power indices is the Shapley-Shubik power index. In this article, this index is used as a 'proxy' for the degree of control held by a particular shareholder. 

The proposed method is sufficiently straightforward to be applied in valuations in the context of closed relationships. A possible drawback of the method is that it requires an estimate of the shareholder value of the company, assuming it is optimally managed. Such an estimation inherently involves a certain degree of subjectivity.

title: From the Local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Limit to Global Trapping for Critically-Scaled Online SGD
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania and University of Southern California

detail.title: From the Local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Limit to Global Trapping for Critically-Scaled Online SGD

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No declaration
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is not a study with patients/participants

detail.abstract: Rangriz (2026) studies online SGD on single-index models at the critical step-size scaling δ N = 1/N. At this scaling the ballistic (ODE) limit of the correlation m = ⟨x, x * ⟩ is degenerate: started from m 0 = 0 it stays exactly at m ≡ 0 (Corollary 2.5), and the fate of SGD near this fixed point is instead governed by a diffusive correction. After rescaling ˜︁ m = √ N m, Rangriz shows that near a stable fixed point r * ⊥ of the (non-degenerate) radius dynamics, ˜︁ m converges to an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and-crucially-proves that its drift coefficient θ(r * ⊥) is always strictly positive (Corollary 2.7), for any bounded activation with information exponent k ≥ 2. This is a new, purely local phenomenon: it describes fluctuations of ˜︁ m on the microscopic scale O(1), over O(N) SGD steps, but says nothing by itself about whether or when SGD reaches macroscopic (weak) recovery m = Ω(1). This note closes that gap. Since the drift is unconditionally positive, the local SDE is a stable, stationary Gaussian process, and a Borell-TIS-type tail bound shows that on any polynomial-inN number of SGD steps, m stays O(N-1/2+ε) with probability 1-o(1): the local diffusive mechanism predicts trapping, uniformly across every information exponent k ≥ 2, with no repelling regime of any kind. This sharpens-and in one respect simplifies-the qualitative BGJ picture (linear/quasi-linear/polynomial recovery time, depending on k, away from this scaling): at the exact critical step size, all of that structure collapses, and recovery cannot be explained by the local diffusive limit alone at any information exponent. We work out the drift coefficient explicitly for phase retrieval, where it evaluates to θ(r ⊥) = 6r 2 ⊥ , confirming positivity directly, and we state as a conjecture the two ways recovery could still occur: a large-deviation escape governed by higher-order (beyond-quadratic) corrections to the drift, or a departure from the exact critical step size that restores the classical ballistic mechanism. Contents 1 Introduction 1 2 Setup and recollection of the local limit 2 3 Universal trapping at the critical step size 3 4 Worked example: phase retrieval 4 5 Conclusion 5

title: They knew before you Did: Addressing Ethics and Economic Trust in the Face of Political Insider Trading

detail.title: They knew before you Did: Addressing Ethics and Economic Trust in the Face of Political Insider Trading

declarations.funderStatement: No funding needed

detail.abstract: In April 2012, Congress passed the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act, prohibiting members from trading securities based on material, nonpublic information gained through their official position. Despite this prohibition, congressional trading activity continues to raise questions about whether members still profit from privileged access to information, and whether existing enforcement is sufficient to prevent it. This research examines the extent and implications of political insider trading and evaluates reforms that could restore public trust in Congress and confidence in financial markets. A meta-analysis of congressional trading data spanning four decades was conducted to assess abnormal returns potentially attributable to the use of privileged information. The results show that political figures consistently earn abnormal returns linked to information obtained through their congressional position. This study finds that measured abnormal returns fell from 85 bps per month pre-STOCK Act to approximately-7 bps post-STOCK Act (Belmont et al., 2022), indicating that disclosed congressional trading no longer shows a statistically detectable informational advantage in the reviewed post-Act sample-though this does not rule out undetected trading occurring outside disclosed channels or asset classes. The findings further suggest that stronger transparency and enforcement measures could reduce this pattern. By tracing STOCK Act enforcement across multiple Congresses, this research offers legislators concrete guidance for strengthening accountability.

title:
Algorithmic Verification and Preventive Automation in Legal Intake: Mitigating Operational Risk and Enhancing Compliance in Electronic Filing Systems 
Integrating Rule-Based Systems and Automated Pre-Filing Audits to Ensure Document Reliability in Modern Legal Engineering
affiliations: Florida International University

detail.title:
Algorithmic Verification and Preventive Automation in Legal Intake: Mitigating Operational Risk and Enhancing Compliance in Electronic Filing Systems 
Integrating Rule-Based Systems and Automated Pre-Filing Audits to Ensure Document Reliability in Modern Legal Engineering
detail.abstract: The rapid evolution of legal technology has shifted document management from passive electronic storage toward automated, algorithmic workflow optimization. However, electronic court filing (e-filing) infrastructures remain exposed to operational vulnerabilities caused by unverified pre-filing submissions. This paper investigates the integration of rule-based algorithmic verification and automated pre-filing audits into legal intake workflows. By examining the intersection of legal informatics, risk management, and professional responsibility standards, we demonstrate how automated cross-field validation, Optical Character Recognition (OCR) metadata extraction, and structural rule engines mitigate operational risk, eliminate clerk correction queues, and ensure strict compliance with court filing rules. We present an algorithmic model within the Procedural Integrity Framework (PIF) and establish ethical safeguards under human-in-the-loop oversight principles.

title: Public Health and Economic Burden of a Proposed 3,500-MW Natural Gas Plant in Virginia: A PM2.5 Dispersion and Impact Analysis
affiliations: Bocconi University, Harvard University - Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health, Harvard University - Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health and Harvard University - Department of Biostatistics

detail.title: Public Health and Economic Burden of a Proposed 3,500-MW Natural Gas Plant in Virginia: A PM2.5 Dispersion and Impact Analysis
detail.abstract: Rapid growth in electricity demand driven by data centers is accelerating proposals for new fossil fuel power generation in the United States, often with limited assessment of associated public health impacts. We conduct a health and economic impact assessment of a proposed 3,500 MW natural gas-fired power plant developed by Balico LLC in Pittsylvania County, Virginia, quantifying the power plant-attributable fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emissions, regional dispersion, population exposure, and associated health and economic burdens. Emissions estimates were derived from operational data from comparable natural gas turbines, dispersion was modeled using the Intervention Model for Air Pollution (InMAP), and health and economic impacts were estimated using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's CO-Benefits Risk Assessment (COBRA) tool. We estimate that the proposed facility would emit approximately 326.5 tons of PM2.5 annually, increasing exposure for more than 1.2 million people across Virginia and North Carolina; over 17,600 residents of Pittsylvania County would experience plant-attributable PM2.5 increases exceeding 0.1 microgram per cubic meter, on top of background concentrations near 8 microgram per cubic meter. These exposures are associated with estimated annual health-related economic damages ranging from $31 million to $65 million, disproportionately affecting older, lower-income, and racially marginalized communities. Following public dissemination of these findings, the proposed project was withdrawn, underscoring the policy relevance of transparent, spatially resolved health impact assessments for informing energy siting and permitting decisions with regional consequences.

title: Prioritizing Best Average Outcomes Leaves the Most Vulnerable Exposed Under Climate Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Zaragoza, University of Zaragoza, Fundación Nueva Cultura del Agua, Centro de Investigaciones Biológicas del Noroeste, S.C. and Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche

detail.title: Prioritizing Best Average Outcomes Leaves the Most Vulnerable Exposed Under Climate Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Managing the resilience of social-ecological systems under climate change is a central challenge of sustainability science. Yet how acting on resistance, adaptability, and transformability affects different system components and how these effects vary under contrasting climate scenarios remain empirically underexplored. Here, we use a simulation model grounded in long-term place-based research in a declining dryland social-ecological system to assess these effects on human population and livestock numbers under climate change uncertainty. Acting on transformability produces the best average outcomes under favorable climate conditions. However, under unfavorable ones, transformation alone is insufficient to prevent system decline: livestock farming collapses in the worst simulations, exposing the households most dependent on it. Acting on resistance consistently avoids this outcome. The choice of which capacity to prioritize has uneven consequences across system components and actors, asymmetries that place-based research paired with dynamic modeling can make visible and that risk-aware resilience governance must address.

title: Optimal Irreversible Consumption with Fixed Utility Adjustment Costs
affiliations: Kyung Hee University - Department of Applied Mathematics  and Sungshin Women's University

detail.title: Optimal Irreversible Consumption with Fixed Utility Adjustment Costs
detail.abstract: We study optimal consumption and portfolio choice in a complete continuous-time market when the consumption standard is irreversible and each upward revision causes a fixed loss of utility. The fixed charge makes adjustment lumpy and destroys pointwise concavity in impulse policies, so market completeness alone does not deliver the usual martingale duality. We establish value strong duality by using arbitrarily short, spanned Brownian lotteries to convexify the closure of attainable expenditure-utility pairs, and we state separately the conditions required for optimizer and portfolio recovery. The dual problem is a two-state impulse-control problem. For logarithmic utility, additive scale invariance reduces it to one dimension and yields an analytical solution characterized by a unique scalar equation, together with a trigger-target policy, budget-matching multiplier, and primal solution. For power utility, we obtain a sharp well-posedness criterion, a monotone finite-intervention construction, dynamic programming and viscosity characterizations, and a verification theorem that establishes feedback admissibility without a separately imposed transversality condition. We also derive the free-boundary relations and explain why local contact conditions are not sufficient. A matched-root specification admits a verified closed-form last-adjustment region, while a monotone discrete QVI treats the remaining and generic cases. Closed-form benchmarks quantify the fixed-grid numerical error.

title: Introducing Fluorescence Heterogeneity to Augment Sample-Based Training Data for 3D Cell Segmentation
affiliations: University of Warwick, University of Warwick and University of Warwick

detail.title: Introducing Fluorescence Heterogeneity to Augment Sample-Based Training Data for 3D Cell Segmentation
detail.abstract: Synthetic cell image modelling offers an alternative to the hand-annotated datasets required for training deep learning models for 3D cell image analysis. However, generative frameworks for 3D cell imaging remain relatively underdeveloped, limiting their broader application. In previous work, we established a sample-based image generation framework that achieved accurate segmentation performance for cells with radially distributed fluorescence. Here, we extend this framework to capture heterogeneous fluorescence patterns on cell surfaces, thereby increasing the scope of models trained on synthetic data. To achieve this, we developed novel image augmentation methods based on Perlin noise that simulate biologically and experimentally relevant patterns commonly observed in fluorescence microscopy. By incorporating these augmentations into the sample-based image generation process, we demonstrate that synthetically trained segmentation models exhibit improved robustness and generalisation when applied to real cell images with heterogeneous fluorescence patterns.

title: University of California System Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) Readability Report

detail.title: University of California System Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) Readability Report

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This report examines the readability and linguistic complexity of Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) policies published across nine University of California institutions as of August 15, 2026. The analysis applies four established readability measures—the Automated Readability Index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, and SMOG—along with measures of policy length, lexical diversity, complex-word use, and sentence length. Findings reveal substantial variation in both the amount and difficulty of SAP information students must navigate. Policy length ranged from 481 words at UC Merced to 3,275 words at UC Berkeley, while the proportion of complex words ranged from 17.8% to 24.9%. Sentence-level analysis also identified lengthy constructions that may increase comprehension demands. Overall, the findings demonstrate uneven accessibility of SAP communication across the UC system and highlight opportunities to improve clarity through shorter sentences, direct language, and more student-centered explanations of financial aid eligibility requirements.

title: The NAIERM Framework: A Technical Primer

detail.title: The NAIERM Framework: A Technical Primer

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence raises the efficiency of human production while routing a growing share of the resulting income from labor to capital. Because the labor and capital circuits recirculate income at very different rates-a marginal propensity to consume of roughly 0.85 for labor income against a marginal propensity to invest near 0.35 for machine income-that routing withdraws demand from the economy even as productive capacity expands. This primer frames the problem not as one of distribution but of regulation specifically, holding capacity utilization at a desired setpoint. This is a constrained optimization problem where the economy functions at its overall best the closer the controls can manage to the target. 

The model defines a self-normalizing index (the GDP Divergence Index) that meters the routing in near-real time; a single coupling parameter (the Spending Circulation Factor, φ) that converts the income split into an economy-wide re-spend fraction; and a closed-loop instrument (the OASIS circuit) that holds capacity utilization at a measured setpoint by cycling a use-blind compute excise back into the consumer circuit as Participation Capital. The control problem has one actuator, one gauge, and one setpoint. The imbalance OASIS corrects is not new with AI; it is a structural condition seen in past revolutions, but those revolutions happened over sufficient time frames to ultimately adjust. The AI transition is happening at a rapid enough pace that doing nothing is unsurvivable. The links in the argument are public metrics, and the framework is falsifiable against what those metrics will show.

title: Closure and Curvature in Sparse Compensated Comparisons
affiliations: Southwest Jiaotong University Hope College

detail.title: Closure and Curvature in Sparse Compensated Comparisons

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO
declarations.funderStatement: No

detail.abstract: This paper studies a sparse compensation experiment. A query fixes a standardized finite gain in one attribute, varies the sacrifice in another, and records the exact threshold at which a binary choice switches. Each queried pair contributes only one number. Under a common increasing-concave additive representation with no pair-specific rescaling, a threshold calibrates one finite utility increment; repeated use of the same attributes across compensation roles makes these calibrations close and generates testable restrictions. We characterize both the support needed for falsification and the realized data needed for bounded relative measurement. First, all positive thresholds are rationalizable under sacrifice-side curvature if and only if the gain-loss incidence graph is a forest; with common concavity across gain and sacrifice roles, the associated quotient digraph must also be acyclic. Second, with at most two observed knots per compensator, sharp ratio bounds are exactly weighted-path bounds. The third knot is the first point at which a three-increment secant restriction can generate a backward ratio bound without an ordinary return path. Finally, bounded measurement of n standardized finite gain increments requires at least n exact thresholds; at this minimum size, bounded identification is equivalent to full tie rank and a spanning directed cycle of successor links. The results separate calibration from testability and show how finite curvature can create measurement closure beyond ordinary network topology.

title: Financing Costs, Credit and Capital Formation in Albania: Integrated Reconstruction after Three Tests of the I-I Model
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Financing Costs, Credit and Capital Formation in Albania: Integrated Reconstruction after Three Tests of the I-I Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or non-financial relationships that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, the research reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses publicly available macroeconomic and financial data and does not involve human participants, patients, animals, or personal identifiable data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the relationship between financing costs, credit and gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) in Albania in the quarterly period 2006Q4-2025Q4. The analysis uses the logarithm of gross fixed capital formation as a dependent variable, the logarithm of gross domestic product (GDP) and the consumer price index (CPI) as macroeconomic controls, spreads as indicators of the relative financing cost, and credit-to-GDP ratios as measures of financial intensity. The autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL)/unrestricted error-correction model (UECM) approach is used because the variables have mixed order of integration and the sample is limited. The results support the cost of capital channel: spreads are negatively related to investment and retain consistent interpretation in alternative specifications. The credit channel is interpreted with caution: credit-to-GDP ratios look more convincing as indicators of leverage, the denominator effect or balance sheet stress than as a pure positive funding channel. The evidence for the financial accelerator is partial because direct series on firm balance sheets, collateral and bank portfolio quality are missing. The main contribution is the reconstruction of a conditional macrofinancial argument for the Albanian case, where bank-based financial structure and euroization make monetary transmission more complex than in the standard interest rate model. A sectoral extension based on INSTAT quarterly construction gross value added real growth is added as a production-side robustness check, with careful distinction between sectoral co-movement and structural causality.

title: The Depreciation of Understanding: An Idea-community Measurement Proposal for Activation Capability

detail.title: The Depreciation of Understanding: An Idea-community Measurement Proposal for Activation Capability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NONE
declarations.funderStatement: NONE

detail.abstract: Endogenous growth theory identifies ideas as the central engine of long-run economic growth, distinguished from physical capital by non-rivalry: one person's use of an idea does not diminish another's. This paper argues that a community's capacity to activate an idea-to reconstruct why it works and how to reproduce it-is a separable variable from the idea's bare existence, and that several existing literatures already document pieces of this phenomenon without yet treating it as a unified, measurable state variable. Organizational-forgetting research shows learned productive knowledge depreciating for reasons unrelated to competitive displacement; research on tacit knowledge documents technologies that become effectively "uninvented" when the community capable of reproducing them dissolves, even as symbolic records survive; and R&D-capital depreciation research measures a related but analytically distinct phenomenon-economic depreciation inferred from productivity, market value, and obsolescence rather than direct measurement of activation capability. Drawing on this series' account of measurement conventions as prior theoretical commitments (Paper 1), navigational validity for open systems (Paper 2), Interpretive Entropy as the mechanism by which reasoning coherence degrades in fragmented systems (Paper 3), the non-linear threshold dynamics of that degradation (Paper 4), the resulting unmeasured economic cost (Paper 5), and understanding as a sustained field-relationship rather than a possessed object (Paper 6), this paper proposes continuity capital as an idea-indexed measure of activation capability whose discriminant validity against organizational forgetting, tacit-knowledge, organization-capital, and absorptive-capacity measures remains unestablished. The claim is offered as a synthesis and formalization proposal, not a discovery, and a second adversarial review of this paper's own reasoning concluded that its residual novelty is not yet demonstrated at the level of mechanism-only at the level of unit of analysis (indexing activation capability to an idea-community pair rather than to a firm, a patent, or an organization). That conclusion is accepted here rather than resisted: applying this paper's own Condition 5 (Section IV) to itself, the honest current classification is a provisional measurement frame, not yet a validated distinct economic state variable.

title: Using AI in Research: A Case Study in Macroeconomics Illustrating the Advantages and Potential Pitfalls
affiliations: FV OpenRatings

detail.title: Using AI in Research: A Case Study in Macroeconomics Illustrating the Advantages and Potential Pitfalls

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: self

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence in the form of Large Language Models and their agentic wraparounds has advanced to point where AIs can identify and acquire relevant data, can set out hypotheses and models, can identify empirical tests of these, can carry out the tests and analyse results, and can generate complete academic papers. Does this represent a great advance or a great danger for the future of theoretical and/or empirical research? While some advances are known to have been made with the assistance of AI it remans unclear to what extent unguided AI is capable of carrying out and reporting its own research efforts unaided by human guidance. This paper illustrates the issues by reporting research proposed by and executed by an AI (ChatGPT) on a specific live research area. We take a fundamental question in macroeconomics: what causes business cycles?, and put this to the AI. We only ask the initial research question; no further guidance on how to progress the research is supplied by human users. Having allowed the AI to complete several phases of its own research we then request it to write a complete academic paper suitable for journal publication. The results illustrate both the insights and the errors that can result from questioning an assistant AI, much in the same way that Plato illustrated such outcomes in his Meno (2400 BC).

title: Composition Shift and the Measurement of Bias in a Growing Prediction Market: Evidence from Kalshi, 2021-2026

detail.title: Composition Shift and the Measurement of Bias in a Growing Prediction Market: Evidence from Kalshi, 2021-2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interest. The author does not trade on Kalshi, holds no positions on the venue studied, has no financial or personal relationship with the exchange or with the authors of the work replicated, and received no funding for this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Prediction markets are now studied intensively enough that their own growth has become a measurement problem. Using 376.8 million Kalshi fills through June 2026, we show that sports contracts went from 0.009% of the in-scope sample in calendar 2024 to 58.8% after May 2025, and that 41% of the aggregate change in the Mincer-Zarnowitz slope at that boundary is composition rather than any change in how the market prices risk. The natural before/after design across early 2025 largely measures the arrival of an asset class. We then ask the persistence question properly. Reconstructing Kalshi's fee schedule from sixteen dated captures of its own published document, we find the 2025 maker fee was not the exchange-wide regime change the literature assumes: a per-series surcharge covering 8.0% to 14.4% of in-scope markets, revised five times, flat per contract before it was quadratic in price. That rules out a step dummy and calls for a difference-indifferences between treated and untreated series trading in the same months. The pre-specified estimate is a tight null:-0.0016 (0.0064) on 98 treated series. An event study added after that result was known supports parallel trends (χ 2 (5) = 3.24, p = 0.66) and, read as exploratory, indicates a transitory reduction three to four months after a series is charged. The maker's return advantage at prices at or above 50c survives every plausible fee rate. We publish the fee history, the category mapping and the full pipeline.

title: The Insurance Value of Marriage: Alimony restrictions and Household Labor Supply

detail.title: The Insurance Value of Marriage: Alimony restrictions and Household Labor Supply

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicting interests
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received

detail.abstract: This paper studies how households respond when legal insurance for marital specialization is reduced. Alimony protects spouses against the economic losses associated with divorce and therefore affects incentives while marriages remain intact. I exploit the 2008 German alimony reform and compare married couples with unaffected cohabiting couples. Economically dependent spouses increase labor-market attachment following the reform, with employment rising by 4 to 8 percentage points and market work replacing housework rather than leisure. The response is symmetric across gender: dependent husbands and dependent wives adjust similarly, while primary earners do not respond. Heterogeneity analyses and mechanism tests show that the response is not systematically related to marital satisfaction, preference mismatch, or household decision-making power, and only weakly related to predicted divorce risk. Instead, adjustment is concentrated among spouses whose livelihoods rely most heavily on the marriage. The findings suggest that alimony operates as insurance for relationship-specific specialization and that reducing such protection induces households to substitute private earning capacity for legal insurance.

title: Commodity Prices and Currency Tail Risk in Developing Countries
affiliations: City St George's, University of London, University of Leeds - Faculty of Business, , University of Leeds, King’s College London and Overseas Development Institute (ODI)

detail.title: Commodity Prices and Currency Tail Risk in Developing Countries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by the MDB Challenge Fund.

detail.abstract: We examine how global commodity price booms and busts shape currency tail risk in low-and middle-income countries. Combining panel quantile regressions with local projections for 78 countries over 1990Q1-2022Q4, we estimate the effect of commodity price cycles on the 95th percentile of the distribution of quarterly depreciations against the US dollar. At the median, commodity booms are associated with currency appreciation, confirming the conventional commodity-currency relationship. However, this relationship reverses at the tail of the distribution, where commodity booms raise the risk of large future depreciations. This predictive effect is unrelated to the share of commodities in exports, and is stronger the larger the share of non-bank foreign investors in domestic government bond markets. The results point to a financial channel in which yield-seeking non-resident investors amplify currency depreciations once a commodity boom unwinds. Our findings imply that commodity price booms are periods in which to prepare for elevated currency risk.

title: Liquidity as a Condition of Survival: The Collapse of the Signa Group and the Lessons for Investors in Illiquid Assets

detail.title: Liquidity as a Condition of Survival: The Collapse of the Signa Group and the Lessons for Investors in Illiquid Assets

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the collapse of the Signa Group between 2023 and 2026the largest insolvency in recent Austrian economic history: across all proceedings, claims of some 27.6 billion euros were filed. Writing from the perspective of a financial analyst and drawing exclusively on publicly available information, the paper asks whether holding more liquidity would have prevented the collapseand what the case teaches about assets that are hard to exit, about concentration risk, valuation discretion and high leverage. 

The analysis traces the group structure with its roughly one thousand companies, describes how funds were raised from large investors, bonds, secured property loans and profit participation certificates, and assesses the interaction-described in press investigations and analyses-between intra-group rents, fair-value revaluations and the borrowing built upon them. The counterfactual test yields the following result: more liquidity would probably have prevented or substantially mitigated the collapse in its specific form-an uncontrolled cascade of insolvencies from November 2023 onwards; without lower leverage, fixed-rate funding and more resilient structures, however, a severe crisis of adjustment would have been unavoidable even with larger cash holdings. 2

 From the comparison with private equity investments, open-end and closed-end real estate funds and other asset forms that are difficult to value, conclusions for investors are derived: partial commitments rather than full investment, a long investment horizon, acquisition preferably during periods of weakness at a discount-and a liquidity reserve that is never sacrificed to the pursuit of return.

title: The Impossible Trinity of Time-series Validation: A Conservation Law among Training Sufficiency, Test Coverage, and Temporal Causality
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Impossible Trinity of Time-series Validation: A Conservation Law among Training Sufficiency, Test Coverage, and Temporal Causality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: Practitioners validating models on time series — financial data in particular — want three things at once: training sufficiency (each training run uses as much of the sample as possible), test coverage (test sets jointly cover as much of the sample as possible), and temporal causality (training data precede test data). We prove these three demands form a genuine impossible trinity. First, a conservation law: every strictly causal validation scheme satisfies α + β ≤ 1, where α is the worst-fold training fraction and β the test coverage, and expanding-window walk-forward schemes exactly trace the Pareto frontier of this region. Second, a quantitative version: the only currency that buys a violation of the law is anti-causal training mass Λ — every scheme satisfies α + β ≤ 1 + Λ, with k-fold cross-validation attaining equality. Third, a statistical characterization: via a β-mixing decoupling inequality, the leakage bias at a test point is bounded by 2M·β_mix(δ), where δ is the distance from the test point to the first training point lying in its future. Harm is thus governed by the severity of a causality violation, not its volume — which explains why purged k-fold with an embargo works: it trades the hard volume constraint for a soft severity constraint that the memory decay of the data-generating process can drive to zero. The hardness of the trinity equals the memory of the process: it vanishes in the i.i.d. limit, can be bought back at an O(mh/T) sample cost under finite memory, and the part of causality demanded by non-stationarity cannot be bought back by any embargo. We quantify the statistical price of each vertex (leakage bias, learning-curve bias, variance and regime sampling), combine them into a statistical impossibility theorem, and verify each law numerically — including shuffled 5-fold cross-validation reporting an information coefficient of +0.32 for a nearest-neighbor model on pure noise.

title: Two Sides of the Coin: The Interlocking Burden of Income Poverty and Time Deprivation
affiliations: and

detail.title: Two Sides of the Coin: The Interlocking Burden of Income Poverty and Time Deprivation
detail.abstract: Conventional economic frameworks quantify poverty primarily through monetary income or consumption expenditure metrics, overlooking the physical constraint of the 24-hour daily time budget. Grounded in Vickery's (1977) two-dimensional poverty framework and Sen's capability approach, this paper investigates the empirical intersections of income poverty and temporal deprivation using nationally representative data from the National Statistical Office (NSO) Time Use Survey in India under the ICATUS 2016 taxonomy. We operationalize committed work time across paid market production and unpaid domestic and care services to construct a four-quadrant deprivation matrix. Using group-weighted Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and Papke-Wooldridge fractional logit models, the empirical analysis reveals that escaping monetary poverty frequently imposes a substantial temporal penalty. In the middleconsumption tier (𝑄 3), 38.8% of individuals suffer from time poverty by exceeding 10.5 hours of daily committed work, while 41.6% of individuals in the poorest quintile (𝑄 1) remain trapped in dual deprivation. Furthermore, a persistent care penalty ratio exists where women perform 299 minutes of daily unpaid domestic services compared to 26 minutes for men. While moving to the richest quintile (𝑄 5) reduces male daily work burdens by 72.60 minutes, the female reduction is heavily attenuated due to a sticky care constraint (𝛽 = +28.15, 𝑝 < 0.01). In addition, women have an estimated 7.3 percentage point lower discretionary leisure share relative to men. These findings demonstrate that public investments in time-saving basic infrastructure and institutional alignment with the International Labour Organization (ILO) 5R Care Framework are essential to alleviate gendered time poverty and reform social protection targeting.

detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of cloud, open banking APIs, blockchain/DeFi, and large language models (LLMs) has expanded the digital finance attack surface. Yet, evidence on how "new-tech" exposure translates into measurable security risk and financial impact remains fragmented. We propose a Tech-Security Risk Index (TSRI) that integrates (i) exposure to emerging technologies, (ii) vulnerability and dependency metrics, (iii) control strength and governance, and (iv) contemporaneous threat activity. Using a panel of global listed financial firms and a complementary DeFi protocol panel (2011-2025), we combine regulatory disclosures, vulnerability/advisory feeds, text-mined adoption signals, and exploit/incident logs. We estimate panel count and severity models for incidents, event-study effects around disclosures/exploits, volatility responses via GARCH, and a survival model for time-to-the-following-incident. We find that higher new-tech intensity predicts greater short-run incident frequency and loss severity; strong cyber governance and thirdparty assurance attenuate these effects. Market reactions to incidents are adverse and larger when TSRI is high, while audited protocols exhibit lower exploit hazard conditional on complexity and TVL. The TSRI provides a forward-looking, auditable measure that supports risk pricing, supervisory stress testing, and board oversight. Results generalize across jurisdictions and remain robust to alternative index weightings, windows, and selection schemes.

detail.abstract: Despite the potential productivity gains from using draft animals in African agriculture, evidence on the role of cattle rental markets in household production remains scarce. This study examines whether rental markets for draft cattle used in land preparation improve borrower productivity and promote efficient factor allocation, using household survey data from maize farmers in rural Zambia. The results show that cattle borrowers achieve approximately 47% lower maize yields than cattle owners, primarily due to greater production intensification among owners. In contrast, yield differences between borrowers and hand-hoe users are insignificant, suggesting frictions that inhibit efficient allocation. Consistent with this interpretation, less productive farmers are more likely to borrow cattle without payment, indicating that unpaid cattle borrowing serves as a form of social support within agrarian communities. Further analysis shows that both the allocative-efficiency benefits of paid rental and the social-support function of unpaid borrowing are concentrated among farmers located near the village center. Overall, the dual functions of informal cattle rental markets-promoting allocative efficiency and providing social support-are spatially constrained.

title: Interpretive Dependence after Loper Bright: Arvin, County of King, and Downstream Governmental Risk

detail.title: Interpretive Dependence after Loper Bright: Arvin, County of King, and Downstream Governmental Risk

detail.abstract:
Loper Bright is usually discussed as a decision about the allocation of interpretive authority between courts and agencies. This Essay focuses instead on a downstream problem: what happens when state and local governments have already organized programs, budgets, permits, or legal obligations around a federal statutory premise they do not control.

Using two August 2026 Ninth Circuit decisions—Committee for a Better Arvin v. U.S. EPA and County of King v. Turner—the Essay develops the concept of “interpretive dependence.” It identifies two distinct mechanisms through which that dependence can arise. Regulatory incorporation occurs when a federal statutory interpretation becomes embedded in a cooperative-federalism program before judicial correction. Subsequent federal conditioning occurs when state or local commitments precede a later federal assertion of statutory authority to impose new grant conditions.

The Essay argues that these mechanisms expose a dimension of post-Loper Bright risk that conventional court-agency analysis can miss. It also proposes a source-tracing inquiry for identifying the legal status of the federal premise, the path through which it entered a state or local program, and the commitments that depend on it.

title: Tax Incentives and Retirement Savings Choices in Mumbai: An Exploratory Secondary-Data Analysis, 2015-2024

detail.title: Tax Incentives and Retirement Savings Choices in Mumbai: An Exploratory Secondary-Data Analysis, 2015-2024
detail.abstract: This study examines how tax-favoured retirement instruments and demographic differences are associated with retirement-saving choices in Mumbai over 2015-2024. The analysis synthesises public institutional evidence and the manuscript's compiled Mumbai indicators for Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), Public Provident Fund (PPF), National Pension System (NPS), Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS), and insurance. In addition to descriptive comparisons, the revised analysis reports absolute and percentage changes, compound annual growth rates (CAGR), changes in instrument shares, contribution to aggregate growth, a chi-square goodness-of-fit diagnostic, and an ageby-instrument association test with effect size. NPS records the strongest growth (CAGR 19.58%), followed by ELSS (11.32%); together they account for 51.56% of the increase in the compiled indicator between 2015 and 2024. The 2024 instrument distribution is strongly non-uniform (chi-square = 54.43, p < .001; Cohen's w = .513). Using the age-by-instrument frequency table reported in the source manuscript, retirement instrument choice is also associated with age (chi-square = 63.13, p < .001; Cramér's V = .390). Younger respondents are relatively more represented in ELSS, while insurance is disproportionately represented among seniors. These patterns are consistent with the broader literature showing that tax incentives can affect portfolio allocation but do not necessarily create equivalent amounts of new saving. The study therefore concludes that tax incentives should be combined with simpler product design, financial literacy, and clearer communication of the old-and new-tax-regime implications. Because the evidence is aggregated and partly compiled, these findings are associative and exploratory rather than causal.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of evangelical Christianity has transformed Brazilian politics and is commonly associated with rising moral conservatism and support for the political right. Yet the evangelical field is also undergoing profound internal change. We examine the rise of desigrejados-evangelicals who maintain Christian beliefs while remaining unaffiliated with any formal congregation. Building on theories of religious individualisation, we argue that this phenomenon is better characterised as "believing without bonding": individuals retain doctrinal commitment and religious practice while rejecting durable institutional attachment to a single church. Using an original quotabalanced online survey of Brazilian adults (N = 1,514), we estimate that desigrejados constitute approximately 5% of the population and 18% of evangelicals. They remain highly religious but express less conservative moral attitudes and weaker support for the far right in elections than congregational evangelicals. These findings suggest that institutional attachment, rather than evangelical identity alone, shapes political attitudes and behaviour.

title: 2050 and Beyond: Future Transboundary Flood Risk from Nepal to Bihar under Climate Change

detail.title: 2050 and Beyond: Future Transboundary Flood Risk from Nepal to Bihar under Climate Change

detail.abstract: Flooding in northern Bihar is commonly discussed as a recurring regional disaster, yet the geographical processes that generate and shape these floods extend well beyond the administrative boundaries of the state. The Kosi, Gandak and Bagmati river systems connect the Himalayan and foothill environments of Nepal with the densely populated alluvial plains of Bihar. This upstream-downstream relationship creates a distinctive form of transboundary flood risk in which climatic events in one country can influence hydrological conditions and social vulnerability in another. Climate change is likely to make this relationship more uncertain by altering the intensity and distribution of precipitation, temperature regimes, snow and glacier processes, river discharge and the frequency of hydro-meteorological extremes. This article examines the future of Nepal-Bihar transboundary flood risk towards 2050 and beyond. It develops an integrated analytical framework combining climate hazard, hydrological response, downstream exposure, social vulnerability and adaptive capacity. Particular attention is given to the Kosi, Gandak and Bagmati basins and to the flood-prone districts of northern Bihar. The study deliberately avoids dependence on remote-sensing observations and instead proposes a framework based on meteorological records, river-gauge observations, historical flood databases, CMIP6 climate projections, census information, agricultural and livelihood indicators, infrastructure data and field-level household evidence. 1 The existing literature provides several reasons for concern. Climate modelling for the Kosi basin indicates substantial future warming, changes in seasonal precipitation and altered hydrological regimes, including increases in large-flood days under higher-emission scenarios. More recent CMIP6 research projects marked intensification of precipitation extremes in the Kosi basin under both SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, with stronger changes under the latter scenario. At the downstream end, Bihar has experienced substantial spatial and temporal variation in rainfall, while district-level studies demonstrate pronounced differences in flood vulnerability associated with exposure, sensitivity, income, education and adaptive capacity. The article argues that future flood risk in Bihar should not be understood simply as an increase in water arriving from Nepal. Rather, it should be understood as a compound outcome of changing upstream climate, river behaviour, local rainfall, floodplain exposure, agricultural dependence, socioeconomic inequality and institutional preparedness. A 2050 perspective therefore requires a shift from reactive flood control towards anticipatory, climate-informed and transboundary risk governance. The paper concludes that improved real-time information exchange, basin-scale forecasting, climate-resilient infrastructure, socially differentiated vulnerability assessment, agricultural adaptation and stronger Nepal-India institutional cooperation will be central to reducing future flood losses.

title: From Digital Financial Inclusion to Retirement Preparedness: An Exploratory Study of FinTech Adoption among Urban Professionals in Mumbai

detail.title: From Digital Financial Inclusion to Retirement Preparedness: An Exploratory Study of FinTech Adoption among Urban Professionals in Mumbai
detail.abstract: Digital financial inclusion has widened access to payments, investment platforms, and app-based financial services in India, but the extent to which such access translates into long-term retirement preparedness remains less clear. This exploratory study examines FinTech awareness, adoption for retirement-related purposes, behavioural barriers, and self-reported retirement preparedness among 62 urban professionals in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. The study uses a cross-sectional survey and reports descriptive statistics together with Fisher's exact test and a chi-square test of independence. The reported awareness-adoption association is positive in direction but not statistically significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.1738). Behavioural barriers are significantly associated with FinTech adoption (χ² = 13.20, df = 4, p = 0.0104), indicating that trust, digitalfinancial literacy, perceived complexity, and preference for traditional channels may constrain the transition from digital access to sustained retirement-oriented use. A statistical audit of the supplied output also shows that the originally reported independent-samples t-test does not constitute a valid user-versus-non-user comparison because it compares the coded adoption variable with the retirement-satisfaction score; the groupdifference claim therefore requires re-estimation from the respondent-level dataset. The study contributes exploratory micro-level evidence from an underexamined Indian metropolitan setting and highlights the need to distinguish digital access from meaningful long-term financial engagement.

detail.abstract: Primary care physicians have long served as “gatekeepers,” authorizing or withholding patient access to specialty care to control cost and reduce unnecessary utilization. Three decades of research show mixed results, even as this role has migrated from the physician’s office to insurer utilization-management departments and, increasingly, to algorithms. This analytic review distinguishes access to care from insurance coverage, traces the gatekeeper model’s origins, and weighs the evidence for and against its continued use, illustrated with process-flow comparisons and a first-person account of a twelve-hour emergency department wait for prior-authorization approval. It examines gatekeeping’s evolution into prior authorization, electronic medical prior authorization (eMPA), and AI-assisted coverage denial; evaluates the Affordable Care Act’s effect on referral gatekeeping; considers telemedicine, concierge, and direct primary care as access-side workarounds; and compares gatekeeping at community health centers versus major medical centers. It closes by weighing the ACA’s uncertain future and the 2026 midterm elections against what each would change about authorization itself. Rather than defending or abolishing gatekeeping outright, this review argues for retiring the authorization-based gatekeeper, human or algorithmic, in favor of a funded, humanly reviewed care-coordinator model calibrated to its setting.

detail.abstract: Digital sovereignty has moved from a niche policy phrase to a design constraint that shapes procurement, architecture, and standards decisions across governments and regulated industries. Yet the term is used inconsistently-sometimes meaning data residency, sometimes operational control, sometimes strategic independence from a handful of foreign technology vendors. This paper opens the Sovereign Digital Infrastructure Series by proposing a precise, layered definition of digital sovereignty and a reference framework that the remaining eleven papers in the series build on. We trace the term's evolution from a data-protection concept to an infrastructure-policy concept, decompose sovereignty into four control planes-data, compute, operations, and governance-and show how existing initiatives (Gaia-X, the EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework, SecNumCloud, India's data localization rules, and national AI compute programs) map unevenly onto these planes, which explains why sovereignty debates so often talk past one another. We present six detailed case studies, address the most common objections to a plane-based framework, examine the economics of sovereignty investment, and conclude with a maturity model, self-assessment checklist, and glossary that organizations and states can use to sequence investment and communicate precisely about what "sovereign" does and does not mean in a given deployment.

detail.abstract: Sovereign cloud" is now a checkbox on public-sector RFPs, but the term describes a wide spectrum of architectures with very different resilience properties. This paper catalogs the technical patterns used to build sovereign cloud platforms-from simple regional isolation to full confidential-computing stacks with local key custody and escrowed operations-and evaluates each against the four-plane framework introduced in SDIS-01. We trace the market and technical history of sovereign cloud offerings, give particular attention to the gap between marketed sovereignty and architecturally verifiable sovereignty, examine eleven detailed case studies including the EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework and France's SecNumCloud qualification, address common objections to the pattern taxonomy, and specify a reference architecture that composes with the compute-sovereignty patterns detailed in SDIS-05 and the zero-trust controls detailed in SDIS-08. We close with an implementation roadmap, a self-assessment checklist, and a glossary for practitioners building or procuring sovereign cloud infrastructure.

detail.abstract: Engine maintenance is the largest and most volatile maintenance cost in a commercial fleet, and the machinery airlines use to fund it (utilization-based maintenance reserves, negotiated rates, shop-visit quotes, and used-engine top-up provisions) can materially understate what overhauls actually cost. This paper isolates the mechanisms that widen the gap between planned and realized cost: workscope creep, the structural spread between an opening quote and the final out-the-door invoice, escalation over an engine's life, and top-up provisions that may be capped or calculated below realized event cost. Its central argument is deliberately bounded. Engine maintenance rarely fails an airline on its own; it becomes the liquidity trigger when reserve shortfalls, correlated removals, material scarcity, and extended turnaround times arrive together at a carrier that is already financially stressed. Lessors and lenders assess the visible measures of airline health well, but technical maintenance exposure, though often tracked at the asset level, is not consistently integrated into airline default analysis or portfolio-level correlation stress tests. The case evidence is graded by strength: Go First is the clearest, Spirit is instructive but multifactorial, and SmartLynx is a candidate case for further investigation. An illustrative Spirit Airlines liquidity bridge (Appendix B) estimates that, measured to the November 2024 petition, the GTF engine shock accelerated the airline's cash depletion by approximately half a quarter, within a modeled range of roughly 0.4 to 0.8 quarters that depends principally on grounded-aircraft contribution and liquidity assumptions.

detail.abstract: China's economic difficulty is best understood as chronic structural decline rather than imminent collapse: a demand-deficient, deflation-prone, demographically contracting economy whose leadership recognizes the diagnosis but declines the rebalancing that would resolve it, because the required measures shift income and authority toward households. This diagnosis is now well established in the peak-China literature. Its policy implications are not. This paper argues that because the decline is substantially endogenous, it cannot be triggered externally, and coercion aimed at rupture tends to consolidate the regime while imposing disproportionate cost on the initiator. It develops a single organizing contribution — a sequencing framework governed by an operationalized stability constraint. The framework holds that the United States must reduce its exposure to China's one instrument of real, currently unhedged coercive force against it, critical-minerals processing, before applying most forms of pressure, with technology denial as an argued exception that races a faster-closing window. The paper confronts the two strongest objections to its decline premise — overcapacity as durable strategic strength, and the preventive-war risk of a pressured peaking power — and specifies indicators that would falsify the assessment.

detail.abstract: This paper examines a shift in the function of tariffs within United States trade policy, from barriers that trade agreements were designed to reduce toward instruments of leverage deployed to extract concessions. Drawing on three cases — the 2018–2020 US–China dispute and Phase One agreement, the renegotiation of NAFTA into the USMCA, and the 2025–2026 US–India tariff escalation and joint statement — the paper traces a recurring sequence: tariffs on trade already liberalized under existing commitments are raised sharply and unilaterally, sustained through months of negotiation, then partially withdrawn as part of a settlement that also secures purchase commitments, tighter rules of origin, or sectoral market access. Two findings follow from the comparison. First, tariff relief itself becomes the concession being traded, and post-settlement tariff levels remain well above pre-dispute baselines: 25 percent duties on roughly $250–300 billion of Chinese goods persisted after Phase One. Second, the concessions obtained through this method have proven weakly enforceable, most visibly in China’s failure to meet the purchase targets that were the agreement’s central deliverable. Read against the weaponized-interdependence literature, the cases suggest that tariff-based coercion differs from network-based coercion in an important respect: it imposes substantial and well-documented costs on the coercing state’s own firms and consumers, which constrains how long the pressure can credibly be sustained.

detail.abstract: The diverse urban characteristics of developing cities necessitate tailored approaches to Transit-Oriented Development (TOD). While TOD is a priority for sustainable urban growth, much of its development has relied on subjective evaluations, particularly in Dhaka, where objective measures have not been fully integrated. To address this gap, this study aimed to calculate a TOD Index focusing on the newly constructed Mass Rapid Transit (MRT). Drawing from a systematic literature review and an expert opinion survey, twelve indicators were identified and assigned weights for calculating the TOD index across 16 MRT stations, utilizing the 6D framework (Density, Diversity, Design, Destination Accessibility, Distance to Transit, and Development Potential). The study collected spatial data from secondary sources and conducted questionnaire survey for primary data. Results revealed that Mirpur-10 achieved the highest TOD index score (0.79), followed by Farmgate (0.78) and Karwan Bazaar (0.76), reflecting their well-developed urban environments with strong transit accessibility, high density, and diverse land use. The TOD index was further validated using a multinomial logit regression (MLR) model examining travel behavior as performance indicator. Outcomes of MLR show that higher TOD index values significantly increase the likelihood of using active and public transport, with people in high-index areas being 11 times more likely to use active transport and 37 times more likely to use public transport than those in low-index areas. Overall findings highlighted four key areas for TOD in Dhaka: enhancing pedestrian-friendly street design and connectivity, promoting mixed-use development, encouraging cost-effective land redevelopment, and redesigning paratransit and busstop facilities.

title: Testing the Predictive Content of Candlestick Formations Under Calibrated Diffusion and Jump Null Processes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Testing the Predictive Content of Candlestick Formations Under Calibrated Diffusion and Jump Null Processes
detail.abstract: Classical Japanese candlestick formations are extensively used as technical trading signals, yet their predictive content relative to memoryless continuous-time stochastic price models remains unclear. This study evaluates six predetermined geometric implementations of canonical candlestick formations across 22 liquid US equities and market ETFs from 2010 to 2025 over holding horizons of 1, 5, 10, and 20 trading days. A calibrated Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) null, with maximum-likelihood parameters and exact Itô drift correction, is used to generate multi-step intraday paths and synthetic Open-High-Low-Close (OHLC) candles. A recursive non-overlapping return sieve is applied to mitigate serial dependence, while distributional differences are assessed using two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests and directional differences using Mann–Whitney U tests with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. The Gaussian GBM null is rejected in 21 of 24 pattern–horizon specifications (p_KS,BH < 0.05), whereas the corresponding rejections largely disappear under a calibrated Merton Jump-Diffusion null (p_KS > 0.12), indicating that jump and tail behavior account for a substantial component of the empirical divergence from GBM. Only four pattern-horizon specifications exhibit significant directional differences after multiple-testing correction. The strongest result occurs for multi-day Bearish Engulfing formations, which exhibit positive forward excess returns ranging from +27.44 bps at h = 5 days to +41.26 bps at h = 20 days. However, pooled panel regressions with calendar-date cluster-robust standard errors show that this effect becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero after controlling for the formation-day return (β_h → 0, p > 0.40), indicating that the apparent signal is attributable to short-term return dynamics rather than independent information in the candlestick geometry. Moving execution from the formation-day close (C_t) to the next-day open (O_t+1) introduces an overnight gap drag of 4.43 to 8.53 bps, which eliminates the remaining economic significance under transaction costs of 5 to 20 bps. These results suggest that canonical candlestick formations provide little independent predictive information beyond underlying return dynamics and are consistent with weak-form market efficiency.

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the equity correlation risk premium — the amount by which option-implied correlation exceeds the correlation subsequently realized — on 5,174 trading days between January 2006 and July 2026, and finds that it has disappeared. Implied correlation is the Cboe COR1M index; realized correlation is the mean pairwise correlation of daily returns on forty large-capitalization S&P 500 constituents over the following 21 trading days. The premium averaged 10.70 correlation points in 2010-2014 and negative 1.86 points in 2022-2026, a difference of 12.56 points with a t-statistic of negative 5.85 and an estimated structural break in November 2014. The trend is negative at all twenty-one non-overlapping sampling offsets and in a circular block bootstrap. The index volatility premium is unchanged over the same period, and decomposing it shows why: the single-stock volatility premium rose from 4.3 to 16.5 points while the correlation premium fell, and implied single-stock volatility rises about twice as fast as realized in every window. Adding today’s largest constituents to the basket leaves that trend intact. Implied correlation down, single-stock implied volatility up and index implied volatility unmoved is the footprint a crowded dispersion book leaves on the surface it trades. Of the 20.2-point fall in implied correlation, 14.7 points are genuine decorrelation and 5.5 points are the premium itself.
