detail.abstract: This study combines web scraping, large language models, and an XLM-RoBERTa model to collect and classify vacancy data from a major Colombian job portal into twenty-eight fields of the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED). Results show that Business and Services fields account for a substantial share of observed vacancies, while employment and job-vacancy rates vary considerably across fields. When the composition of vacancies is compared with the composition of the labor force and higher education enrollment, Business, Services, and Data Base & Networks Design appear to be underrepresented in the labor force and enrollment relative to their shares of classified vacancies.

title: Socio-Environmental Conflicts in Extractive Agricultural Enclaves

detail.title: Socio-Environmental Conflicts in Extractive Agricultural Enclaves
detail.abstract: Rural extractive enclaves are often described as "lawless." But is the law truly absent in these regions? This chapter explores how the law shapes and defines socioenvironmental conflicts in extractive agricultural enclaves. Applying the lens of legal geography, I analyze a set of thirty five case studies of high intensity socioenvironmental conflicts related to the agricultural industry in Latin America. The Chapter examines how law shapes extractive enclaves and mediates socioenvironmental conflicts along the following dimensions: (1) how international trade and investment law property law, and land use regulations influence spatial ordering and craft the geographies of extractive enclaves; (2) how labor law, subsidy policy, and taxation frameworks mold profitability and viability of extractive projects; (3) how legal regulations related to the privatization of security - for example, frameworks that allow for memorandums of understanding between state security forces and private companies, as well as those that govern the creation of private security companies - and the regulation of agrochemicals influence the monopoly of force and violence within extractive enclaves; and (4) how spaces of legal adjudication - including domestic, regional, and international frameworks and fora - mediate socioenvironmental conflicts once they arise. This Chapter concludes that law is not “absent” in rural extractive enclaves, but is instead constitutive of these geographies and selectively deployed therein.

title: Commons Capitalism: A Terminological and Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Commons Capitalism Entity

detail.title: Commons Capitalism: A Terminological and Conceptual Framework for Understanding the Commons Capitalism Entity
detail.abstract:
Commons Capitalism proposes a form of market enterprise whose institutional architecture differs in important respects from the conventional corporation, worker cooperative, employee stock ownership plan, and charitable nonprofit. Understanding the proposal is complicated, however, by the familiarity of the words used to describe it. Terms such as commons, capitalism, corporation, nonprofit, ownership, worker, and benefit carry established meanings and associations that can cause a reader to place the Commons Capitalism Entity (“CCE”) within an existing organizational category before understanding its structure.

This paper therefore precedes detailed examination of the economics, financing, governance, worker benefits, acquisition strategy, and scalability of Commons Capitalism. Its purpose is terminological and conceptual. It defines the principal elements of the CCE, identifies familiar but misleading mental models through which those elements may initially be interpreted, and establishes the conceptual framework necessary for subsequent analysis.

The central proposition is that a CCE is a commons-based enterprise operating within a market economy. The productive institutional wealth generated and renewed through continuing market enterprise is treated as a commons resource. It is administered for multiple institutional purposes through a polycentric governance structure, while no shareholders, members, workers, or other private parties hold a residual ownership claim to the enterprise. Legal title to the assets constituting the CCE’s productive capital is centralized in the Commons Corporation rather than vested in its operating Subsidiaries. Because the resource and the institution are intended to continue beyond any present worker cohort, intergenerational stewardship governs their preservation and use across time. Operating businesses remain subject to markets, competition, profitability requirements, financing constraints, and ordinary economic risk. Growth occurs principally through acquisition of existing healthy businesses, thereby potentially extending the CCE’s employment relationship, wages, benefits, and institutional protections to additional workers.

These features cannot be understood adequately in isolation. They constitute an integrated institutional architecture. A renewing economic resource gives rise to questions of use and preservation; multiple uses and worker cohorts create a governance problem; polycentric governance distributes authority without creating residual ownership; the continuing time horizon gives rise to intergenerational stewardship; stewardship affects capital preservation; capital preservation affects financing and acquisition; and acquisition determines whether the benefits of the enterprise can extend beyond its original worker cohort. Understanding Commons Capitalism therefore requires three levels of comprehension: accurate terminology, understanding of the individual institutional components, and ultimately an integrated understanding of how those components operate together.

title: Cursed Numbers and Blessed Streets: Secularisation and the Fading of Superstition in the UK Housing Market
affiliations: University of Cambridge - Department of Land Economy and University of Cambridge - Department of Land Economy

detail.title: Cursed Numbers and Blessed Streets: Secularisation and the Fading of Superstition in the UK Housing Market
detail.abstract: Britain's secularisation is usually documented through what people say about their beliefs. This paper asks whether it can also be read from what they pay. We study two symbolic address attributes at opposite poles of the Christian tradition, the house number 13, long held to be cursed, and ecclesiastical street names such as Church Lane, which carry the blessing of sacred association. In roughly eight million transactions across Great Britain between 2006 and 2025, both symbols are priced even under tight conditioning, but the effects are small. Number 13 sells at a 0.23 per cent discount to its immediate neighbours, and an ecclesiastical address at a 0.72 per cent premium. These pooled figures mask a clear trend. Both effects stand at roughly 1.5 per cent at the start of the window and erode to zero thereafter. The early discount and premium are concentrated in districts whose Christian share fell least between the 2001 and 2021 censuses, while the fastest-secularising districts appear to have completed the process before 2006. The results read the housing market as an instrument of cultural observation. Surveys record what people profess and transactions record what they pay for. In Britain, the two records of religious decline agree.

title: Sebi's Need of Market Plumbing: Revisiting Settlement Framework in Indian Capital Markets

detail.title: Sebi's Need of Market Plumbing: Revisiting Settlement Framework in Indian Capital Markets
detail.abstract:
At a time when India is striving to retain foreign capital amid persistent FPI outflows and increasing competition from peer markets, the efficiency of our settlement infrastructure may matter as much as our growth story. In this context, my article titled “SEBI’s Need of Market Plumbing: Revisiting Settlement Framework in Indian Capital Markets,” which examines SEBI’s proposed net settlement framework through the lens of market microstructure efficiency and regulatory competitiveness.

The piece argues that settlement architecture is not merely operational design but regulatory infrastructure that may quietly determine the direction of global liquidity flows into India’s markets.

title: Household Insurance on the Job Ladder Spousal Income Loss and Job-to-Job Mobility
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and

detail.title: Household Insurance on the Job Ladder Spousal Income Loss and Job-to-Job Mobility
detail.abstract: We study how involuntary spouse income loss changes employer-to-employer mobility among workers who remain employed. Using linked married couples in SIPP, we show that an involuntary spouse income loss raises the employed worker's wave-to-wave employer mobility by 2.00 percentage points from a 5.63 percent baseline. The response is concentrated in earnings-improving moves and is larger when the spouse supplied a higher pre-shock earnings share. We then estimate a household on-the-job search model in which a spouse shock changes the employed worker's search and acceptance problem through household income. Within the model, the response operates through higher search intensity and a shifted acceptance frontier toward higher current earnings, while some induced moves trade latent amenities for pay. The evidence shows that employer mobility is an adjustment margin through which dual-earner households respond to involuntary spouse income shocks.

title: The Contribution of the 500K Steps Campaign to Nature-Based Recreation and Tourism Development

detail.abstract: The 500K Steps Campaign represents a nature-oriented recreational initiative designed to encourage people to engage in walking, outdoor activity, environmental appreciation, and exploration of natural destinations. This research examines the campaign's contribution to nature-based recreation and tourism development, with particular attention to participation, destination awareness, local economic activity, environmental appreciation, and opportunities for sustainable tourism. A qualitative research approach was adopted, using semi-structured interviews with 50 participants who had knowledge of or experience with the campaign. Interview participants included campaign participants, residents, tourism-related businesses, guides, community representatives, and other stakeholders. The findings indicate that the campaign can contribute to nature-based recreation by encouraging physical activity in outdoor environments, increasing awareness of natural attractions, and creating opportunities for participants to discover less-visited destinations. The research also identifies potential tourism benefits, including increased visitor flows, greater visibility of local destinations, and opportunities for small businesses. However, respondents highlighted challenges related to infrastructure, environmental management, visitor safety, waste management, and the need for stronger coordination among tourism and community stakeholders. Overall, the study suggests that the 500K Steps Campaign can function as a platform for connecting physical activity, nature appreciation, community participation, and tourism development when supported by appropriate destination management and sustainability measures.

title: The Architecture of Trust
affiliations: Pan African University Institute for Governance, Humanities and Social Sciences

detail.title: The Architecture of Trust
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the standard model of international philanthropy that treats African communities as permanent aid recipients. Rather than depending on centralized external welfare, which creates endless dependency, the text argues for decentralizing social security by reviving traditional resource-pooling practices such as Zunde raMambo, stokvels, and Harambee. Communities can build the necessary seed capital through informal savings, diaspora remittances, and profits from informal cross-border trade. To update these systems for today, the author suggests pairing traditional leadership with licensed social workers to guarantee fair distribution. It also recommends using accessible tools like USSD networks and Distributed Ledger Technology to track funds transparently. Finally, tying these local trusts to broader regional frameworks, like the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, turns basic rural safety nets into real drivers of independent wealth and resilience.

detail.abstract: Federal higher education accountability increasingly uses post-completion earnings to determine whether programs remain eligible for federal aid, most notably through the Earnings Premium (EP) established under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) of 2025. This paper examines whether the EP provides sufficient evidence for the high-stakes decisions attached to it. Drawing on Messick's unified validity theory and Kane's argument-based approach, the paper explores the chain of inferences from administrative wage records to program eligibility decisions. The analysis brings concerns about attribution, timing, contextual variation, and equity into a common validity framework, identifying weaknesses and strengths in the links connecting earnings to claims about program performance and eligibility. It concludes with implications for a more defensible accountability design.

title: Sports Barbecue as a New Paradigm of Participatory Sport

detail.title: Sports Barbecue as a New Paradigm of Participatory Sport

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none

detail.abstract: This study does not define Sports Barbecue merely as a combination of barbecue cooking technique and athletic competition. This study proposes Sports Barbecue as a new paradigm of participatory sport that can emerge in an era in which artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and digitalization are transforming human labor and social relationships. Contemporary sport has developed a structure in which spectator sport (Spectator Sport), centered on professional athletes' competition, records, spectatorship, and media consumption, and participatory sport (Participatory Sport), in which humans directly engage in athletic activity, exist in a complementary relationship. A growing body of research indicates that sport participation can carry social value related not only to achievement and physical health but also to psychological well-being, interpersonal relationships, prosocial behavior, and a sense of belonging. However, this study does not limit the meaning of participation to competing in a match alone. In Sports Barbecue, participants engage in the entire process, from the competition itself to preparing and managing the fire, cooking, waiting, competing, observing, conversing, exchanging culture, eating together, and reuniting. Sports Barbecue is therefore proposed as a model that expands the concept of participatory sport from the act of competing to human relationships and communal experience. To explain this structure, this study connects Victor Turner's concepts of liminality and communitas, commensality, research on the social capital and social legacy of sport events, and research on work alienation. Sport event participation has the potential to build social capital composed of trust, networks, and reciprocity, and research exists showing that participatory sport events can produce positive social outcomes for local communities. At the same time, research also shows that such relationships do not automatically develop into a sustainable community from the hosting of a single event. It is precisely at this point that this study proposes the distinctiveness of Sports Barbecue. Rather than expecting community as an outcome, it makes the formation of community itself the design principle of the sport event. Furthermore, drawing on recent research suggesting that, in an age of digitalization and automation, work alienation can be understood as a multilayered phenomenon arising in the individual's relationship with their occupation, with others, and with themselves, this study holds that the value future sport must provide to human beings cannot be explained by athletic performance alone. Accordingly, this study proposes shifting the question about sport from "What do humans do in sport?" to "What do humans gain from sport?" Humans do not gain only victory from sport. Humans can gain recognition, relationships, belonging, growth, shared memory, mutual encouragement, and the strength to live again. Synthesizing these functions, this study proposes a new concept: Human Sanctuary. Human Sanctuary is not an established concept in existing scholarship but a concept proposed by this study; it refers to a social and symbolic space in which a person recognizes the existence of others and is recognized in turn, maintains relationships and belonging even amid competition and failure, and gains the strength to return to reality. The ultimate claim of this study is that Sports Barbecue need not stop at adding one more athletic event; it can become a sociocultural experiment that rediscovers, within the form of sport, the ways in which human beings need one another.

detail.title: A Multimodal Perturbation Atlas Defines the Phenotypic Resolution of Cellular Morphology
detail.abstract: ​Modeling cellular behavior requires measurements that capture how cells evolve across time, environments, and interventions. Microscopy is uniquely suited to this goal: it is non-destructive and can be applied to living cells in their native context. Yet its phenotypic resolving power remains incompletely characterized relative to molecular assays. Here, we present a multimodal perturbation atlas of 1,000 pooled CRISPR knockouts in A549 cells, profiled by fluorescence microscopy (42 live, 13 fixed markers), label-free quantitative phase imaging of the same live cells (at single timepoints), and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). We develop deep learning frameworks to interpret the rich cell-biological signatures in these ~65M single-cell profiles. At matched reagent cost, phase imaging exceeds the phenotypic resolution of both fluorescence imaging and scRNA-seq, and more reliably recovers higher-order pathway organization. These results establish intrinsic morphology as a high-precision readout of cellular state, and lay a foundation for live-cell profiling of phenotypic trajectories.

detail.abstract: This chapter argues that AI economies are constituted through data in motion and the advanced-compute infrastructures that make data actionable. Kitchin et al (2025) identify the mechanisms through which digital data replicate, proliferate and transform; Masso et al (2025a) treat transborder movement as social data migration embedded in institutional, cultural and geopolitical change. These are overlapping rather than separate lenses: digital mechanisms are socio-material, while social transformation includes infrastructures, standards and technical practices. Richard Nelson's contrast between 'the Moon' and 'the Ghetto' supplies the distributive question. In the supercomputing age, states and firms can coordinate frontier models, AI factories and quantum-classical systems while struggling to connect them to dispersed social needs. Evidence from the Dublin/Ireland planning-data ecosystem, Tallinn/Estonia's X-tee and e-Residency ecology, and the Basque Country's advanced-compute strategy shows how replicas, categories, expertise and authority move differently. Geographical hosting and nominal eligibility do not by themselves distribute the To cite this chapter: Calzada, I. (2027) AI Economics and Data In Motion: Between the Moon and the Ghetto. In Rob Kitchin & Anu Masso, Data in Motion. Bristol: Bristol University Press. ability to formulate problems, govern data, interpret results or challenge providers. Reconnecting frontier capability and social purpose requires anticipatory re-embedding across six public capacities, making provenance and dependencies visible, widening effective access, and preserving participation, accountability and reversibility as data and power move across scales.

title: Investigating the Effects of Teff-Sorghum -Fenugreek Flour Blending Ratios on Quality Attributes of Injera

detail.title: Investigating the Effects of Teff-Sorghum -Fenugreek Flour Blending Ratios on Quality Attributes of Injera
detail.abstract: Injera is Ethiopian fermented and leavened flat bread mainly made from teff flour. For improving the protein content and sensory quality of injera, the flours are enriched with fenugreek. Injera made from sorghum flour alone or its blend, however, has noted shortcomings in qualities when compared to teff injera qualities. Therefore this study was carried out to investigate the effects of teff-sorghum - fenugreek flour blending ratios on quality attributes of injera and to optimize the blending ratios of teff, sorghum, and fenugreek flours that give better quality attributes of injera made from these flour formulations. The effects of blending flour ratios on injera quality were investigated using mixture design methodology with a D-optimal design. Fourteen formulations of injera were produced from constrained blends of sorghum (0–50%), teff (50–100%), and fenugreek (0–5%), while a teff flour alone (100% teff flour) injera was served as control. Analyses of response parameters were made using the AACC and AOAC standard methods. Response variables considered in this study were staling rate, proximate, mineral, antinutritional factors and sensory attributes. Proximate compositions (g/100 g) ranged from 56.16 to 69.92 (moisture), 2.64 to 3.91 (ash), 11.36 to 17.19 (protein), 2.258 to 10.838 (fat), 4.179 to 6.988 (fiber) and 59.54 to 77.74 (carbohydrate), and energy, 348.1-385.62 (kcal/100g). Minerals (mg/100 g) varied from Fe: 12.83 to 21.23, Zn: 1.19–2.36, and Ca: 75.26 to 151.13. Antinutritional factors (mg/100 g) varied from 4.106 to0.449 (condensed tannin), 72.83 to 174.84 (phytic acid). Sensory scores for sourness, sweetness, bitterness, softness, stickness, rollability, odour, flavor, eye distribution, color and overall acceptability were 5.00-6.37, 5.14-6.36, 5.24-6.29, 5.14-6.57, 5.14-6.43, 5.93-6.57, 5.57- 6.57, 5.43-6.71, 5.49-6.43, 4.87-6.29 and 5.60-6.23, respectively.3.670 to 4.105(pH) and staling rate (%) varies from 8.95 to 33.43, 9.52 to 34.58, and 12.32 to 52.31 after 24,48 and 72hours, respectively. Alkaline water retention capacity, AWRC (%) varies from 49.42 to 84.01(at zero time), 32.92 to76.49 (after 24 hr), 32.64 to76.01 (after 48 hr), 23.57 to 73.66 (after 72 hr), respectively. Results showed that quality attributes were mainly affected by ingredients and it is possible to prepare better quality attribute injera with a significant fenugreek enrichment without compromising its acceptability by adding in appropriate flour blending ratios. The best blending ratio of injera in terms of overall quality attributes was found 64.1% teff, 32% sorghum and 3.80% fenugreek

title: The Possible Use of Herbs and Spices in the Food Processing and Food Safety
affiliations: Kulumsa agricultural Research center, Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural research, Ethiopia.

detail.title: The Possible Use of Herbs and Spices in the Food Processing and Food Safety
detail.abstract: Spices and herbs are utilised in many different cuisines and food items, but they are consumed in small amounts, making them a special market within the food industry. These plants are rich sources of valuable bioactive components that are utilised for a range of functions, such as flavouring, colouring, medicinal, and preservation. The food industry recognises the potential of plant extracts, and not just because of their nutritional benefits. Antimicrobials and antioxidants, such as various essential oils with antibacterial qualities, are mostly found in plants. Herbs and spices including rosemary, sage, basil, oregano, thyme, cardamom, and clove contain a variety of essential oils. To increase product value and shelf life, plant essential oils are also included as additives to edible or biodegradable films and coatings for active food packaging. However, it is important to consider and thoroughly research any potential harmful consequences of specific phyto-compounds. However, this chapter's findings are more comprehensive, represent significant and timely advances towards potential applications in food sector as well as the food safety aspects of commodities containing spices and herbs by effectively protecting consumers from potential risks resulting from unintentional or intentional contamination of spices and herbs.

title: Competition across the AI Stack: The Need for Humility in a World of Uncertain Monetization
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Management Science (MS)

detail.title: Competition across the AI Stack: The Need for Humility in a World of Uncertain Monetization
detail.abstract: This article argues that it is impossible to think about competition in the AI stack without understanding how each layer of the stack will be monetized, and that in the face of uncertainty about how layers in the AI stack will be monetized, there is a danger that regulators will do two things. First, regulators may focus on the areas of the AI stack where monetization is tried and tested and as a result firms are able to make money, rather than evaluate whether there are structural barriers to entry that could lead to persistent market power. Second, regulators may take monetization models in some layers of the AI stack as given where they are still in an experimental stage, and fail to focus on structural conditions which lead to barriers to entry.

title: Gravity and the Arch: Implementation Tests and Findings

detail.title: Gravity and the Arch: Implementation Tests and Findings

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has professional and ownership interests in businesses related to financial planning, wealth management, and lending. No outside party funded this research or had any role in its design, analysis, conclusions, or publication.

detail.abstract:
The Gravity paper claims a recovered growth rate—the arch—for an investor who holds a baseline allocation and exercises stored safety after damage. This paper tests that claim in simulation, discovers the structure underneath it, and proves what the simulation found.

The arch is an exact long-run law. Under the bang-bang shortfall rule studied here, for baselines below the market the gap to the arch line is positive recurrent with a closed-form stationary law. The fraction of time spent at Kelly converges to (p^* = y_0/(2-y_0)), and mean log-growth converges to the arch. At the market seat, the stationary law disappears and the convergence becomes degenerate.

At the 20- and 50-year horizons tested, the arch is kept by both the median and the dollar mean, but not yet by mean log-wealth: the remaining shortfall is a transient whose clock is computable. Against the natural skeptic—a static portfolio at twice the baseline, or at the best static seat for the same goal—the moving portfolio loses on growth and dispersion and wins on the one thing it was built for: the probability of keeping the line. It does so with less average exposure, and for a computable number of years: 67 at 30/70, 78 at 50/50, 91 at 70/30, and 122 at the market.

The crossover boundary (T^*(y_0)) is exactly characterized—the static side in closed form and the moving side by an explicit Laplace transform—and evaluated numerically as a curve in years. What remains outside the theorem—which paths fall deep, and how deep, before the law asserts itself—is the price. The price is itself a finding: exact, at a price, over time, within limits.

detail.abstract: South Korea has the world's lowest fertility and an intense education race. Families devote nine percent of lifetime income to education, mostly to private tutoring with near-zero measured returns. I show that competition for coveted careers generates an assignment externality: when all families spend more, the admission bar rises and children become costly. In a quantitative model calibrated to this mechanism, replacing score-based assignment with a capacity-preserving lottery raises completed fertility by 0.24 children per couple. Pronatal transfers deliver one eighth of that increase. Education taxes deliver almost none. Preference shifts, not a fiercer race, explain the decline across cohorts.

title: What is Polarisation? A Policy Guide

detail.title: What is Polarisation? A Policy Guide

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA

detail.abstract: This report sets out a six-fold typology to help identify what polarisation is, and, importantly, to predict where we see polarisation arising.  The six-fold typology of polarisation is: (1) refusal of dialogue; (2) framing the other as the enemy; (3) no compromise; (4) monolithic identity; (5) a discourse of danger; and (6) an absolutist ideology. Each is explicated as a distinct aspect of polarisation. Following an examination of the policy implications, the report ends with some suggestions for tackling polarisation, including: use of discourse analysis to spot the potential for polarisation emerging; the need to balance dialogue (early stages) with more prescriptive enforcement against polarised language and groups employing it, but with an awareness that this may be counter-productive yet also aware of the philosopher Karl Popper’s “paradox of toleration”; understanding that not all polarised language/positions are inherently socially harmful; and, the need for education to spot and avoid polarising discourse.

title: Expectation as Ontological Primitive:Rethinking Economic Efficiency and Policy Effectiveness

detail.title: Expectation as Ontological Primitive:Rethinking Economic Efficiency and Policy Effectiveness

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. No funding or personal/financial relationships that could influence this study are reported.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patients, or animals; therefore, ethics approval is not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes that the economy is not primarily governed by material laws but by the resonance of confidence among agents, and it elevates "expectation" to an ontological primitive. It redefines economic efficiency as the smoothness of collaboration (constrained by the finitude of human beings), argues that materialism drives growth only in the scarcity phase and collapses into low desire once abundance crosses a critical threshold, and shows that the effectiveness of institutions and policies rests on inner recognition and narrative management rather than legal form or material manipulation. Wealth is reconceptualized as a claim in social relations whose realization requires the simultaneous presence of claimant and obliged party, while value is the consensus reached by traders—a "consensus theory of value" that clarifies the status of forced transactions, labor, subjective utility, and non-tradable goods. The paper diagnoses modern capitalism as facing an ultimate dead end because it dissolves meaning, and it derives four testable corollaries. The market economy, it concludes, is worthy of esteem precisely because it is the most adequate mechanism for the expression of value consensus—a fact obscured by the instrumentalization of economics.

title: Rerouting Externalities: Flight Diversions and Local Health
affiliations: Wake Forest University - Department of Economics and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Rerouting Externalities: Flight Diversions and Local Health
detail.abstract: Transportation networks absorb disruptions by rerouting activity, shifting local externalities toward communities that did not generate the disruption. We study this rerouting mechanism through flight diversions, linking flight diversion records to neighborhood Emergency Medical Services dispatches in New York City. Using disruptions elsewhere in the air network as an instrument for diversion exposure, we find that greater exposure increases EMS demand, especially in neighborhoods closest to airports and late-night diversions. Delayed scheduled arrivals generate markedly different responses, indicating that spatial reallocation, rather than late arrival alone, contributes importantly to the EMS response. The 2016 relaxation of slot controls at Newark Airport was followed by diversion activity shifting toward the region's other major airports, and higher EMS demand in nearby communities. The findings illustrate how disruptions and airport-capacity policies can redistribute aircraft activity and associated health burdens across connected airports and surrounding communities.

title: Regional Determinants of Foreign Direct Investment in India: The Role of Specialization, Diversification, Competition, and Mobility
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: Regional Determinants of Foreign Direct Investment in India: The Role of Specialization, Diversification, Competition, and Mobility
detail.abstract: This paper studies why foreign firms choose some states over others in India. It focuses on the role of specialization, diversification, competition, and different types of mobility. The results show that competition plays a strong role in attracting investment. Specialization and diversification matter, but their effects are not always consistent. The study also introduces mobility as a new dimension. It looks at labour, capital, and infrastructure mobility separately. Labour mobility has a clear positive effect. States where workers can adjust more easily are more attractive to investors. In contrast, capital mobility does not show a strong influence. Infrastructure mobility shows mixed effects. In some regions, especially in hilly areas, it reflects instability due to environmental conditions. In other regions, it may capture spillover effects from nearby development. Overall, the findings show that mobility is not the same everywhere. Its impact depends on local conditions. This suggests that investment decisions are shaped not only by market structure but also by how regions adjust over time.

title: Robotic Systems Adoption and Cyber Risk in Financial Transactions: An Empirical Analysis of Automation-driven Vulnerabilities in Digital Finance
affiliations: The University of Lahore Islamabad Campus

detail.title: Robotic Systems Adoption and Cyber Risk in Financial Transactions: An Empirical Analysis of Automation-driven Vulnerabilities in Digital Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received to assist with the preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: We studied whether scaling robotic systems adoption (RSAI) raises cyber risk (CRI) in financial transactions and identified the conditions-IT governance (ITG) and regulatory quality (RQ)-that mitigate this risk. We compile a country-year panel for 12 countries from 2014 to 2025 (N = 144). Estimation proceeds from OLS with country-clustered errors to country fixed effects (FE), followed by a dynamic panel System-GMM to address persistence and endogeneity. We examine nonlinearity (quadratic RSAI) and moderation using marginal effects across the distributions of the RQ/ITG variables. Inference uses cluster-robust (and, where feasible, wild-cluster) p-values; GMM diagnostics include AR (2) and instrument controls. Across specifications, RSAI is positively associated with CRI, while ITG is strongly risk-reducing. Interaction and marginal-effects results show that the RSAI→CRI slope is state-dependent, attenuating as RQ/ITG strengthens. The quadratic model suggests a turning point: at low adoption, risk may not rise, but beyond a threshold, additional automation increases CRI unless governance scales accordingly. System-GMM confirms mean reversion in CRI (negative lag) and no AR (2), supporting the identification. Automation programs should be budget-paired with governance upgrades (privileged access, segmentation, monitoring) and staged against risk gates. Regulators can mitigate systemic risk by enhancing RQ (enforcement, disclosure, and third-party rules). We provide the first crosscountry , dynamic evidence that cyber risk is an endogenous by-product of robotic/AI scale, and we quantify how IT governance and institutions reshape this relationship, offering a replicable identification blueprint for digital-risk research.

title: LLMs and OSINT in Digital Commons Governance
affiliations: and University of Delhi

detail.title: LLMs and OSINT in Digital Commons Governance
detail.abstract: The complexity of government policies and welfare schemes usually makes them hard for the average person to understand and access. Poor coordination among communication channels, the slow pace of bureaucracy, and the lack of a central, transparent policy structure worsen the problem, leading to the spread of misinformation and preventing people from making effective use of public services. At the same time, the process of developing policy is hindered by slow decision-making, little public involvement, and a heavy reliance on static datasets rather than on dynamic, real-time intelligence. This article looks at how Large Language Models (LLMs), when smoothly incorporated into the digital commons, can act as an AI-driven mechanism for governance in order to improve policy transparency, accessibility, and cooperation between different departments. By making use of Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT), a government controlled LLM can make sure that policy data stays accurate, is continuously updated, and is available to everyone, thus reducing the need to consult a variety of government websites and unreliable third-party sources. Moreover, predictive analytics and AI-based legislative modelling can improve the policymaking process, allowing governance to become more flexible, forward looking, and responsive to societal needs. Even though the introduction of LLMs into governance offers great possibilities, it is not without difficulties. Issues such as algorithmic bias, the spread of misinformation, financial sustainability, and differences in digital accessibility require the establishment of strong oversight systems, ethical AI governance rules, and clear accountability arrangements in order to address possible risks. Even with all these complications, a careful and thoughtful use of LLMs within the digital commons has the potential to transform public administration by giving the public greater access to policy, improving the efficiency of governance, and promoting real civic participation. This study highlights the need for strategic investments in AI within public administration and calls for a future in which governance is not only technologically supported but also carried out in an inclusive and ethical manner.

title: Valuing the Unprofitable: A Narrative-and-Numbers Framework for Pricing India's New-Age Technology Businesses
affiliations: University of Delhi, Shri Ram College of Commerce, Students

detail.title: Valuing the Unprofitable: A Narrative-and-Numbers Framework for Pricing India's New-Age Technology Businesses

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study relied exclusively on secondary, publicly available data from audited financial statements, regulatory filings, and market exchange records. No human participants or animal subjects were involved in the research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The study was entirely self-funded and conducted independently by the author

detail.abstract: This paper asks a simple but stubborn question: how does one put a rupee value on a business that loses money, disrupts an existing industry, and is priced more on its story than on its statements? Using the framework popularised by Aswath Damodaran, in which a valuation begins with a narrative and is disciplined by numbers rather than the reverse, I build discounted cash flow valuations for three of India's most closely watched new-age technology listings: Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato), One97 Communications (Paytm), and FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa). Each company is walked through a five-stage narrative test covering total addressable market, competitive moat, unit economics, execution risk, and the probability of failure, before these qualitative judgements are converted into explicit revenue, margin, reinvestment, and costof-capital assumptions. The resulting intrinsic values are then compared against actual traded prices to identify the gap, if any, between story-implied value and market price, and to ask what that gap reveals about investor behaviour in India's retail-dominated primary and secondary markets. I find that the three firms sit at different points on the narrative-numbers spectrum: Eternal's story has substantially converged with its numbers as food delivery has matured into a genuine cash-generating business alongside a still-unproven quick-commerce wager; Paytm's turnaround to profitability in FY25 has narrowed, but not closed, a valuation gap inherited from a regulatory shock; and Nykaa continues to trade on the promise of premiumisation more than on the arithmetic of its still-thin margins. The paper concludes that narrative-driven valuation, done honestly and updated as facts change, remains the most defensible way to price young, disruptive, and often unprofitable companies, even when the resulting number is less precise than the market pretends its price to be.

title: Non-Gaussian Stock Price Synchronicity
affiliations: The Open University - Business School

detail.title: Non-Gaussian Stock Price Synchronicity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no personal or financial relationship with other people or organisations that have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: Funded through my employment at the Open University

detail.abstract: Traditional stock price synchronicity measures are based on the coefficient of determination (R²) from a linear market model and therefore capture only dependence explained by linear correlation. We develop a measure of non-Gaussian stock price synchronicity based on mutual information. It is defined as the difference between observed mutual information and the mutual information implied by a Gaussian dependence structure with the same correlation coefficient, and is equivalent to the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the observed and Gaussian copulas. Using a sample of US firms, we show that stock-market dependence frequently exceeds that implied by linear correlation alone and exhibits substantial cross-sectional and time-series variation. Non-Gaussian synchronicity is positively associated with R&D activity and market-to-book ratios and negatively associated with asset tangibility, while traditional measures of downside vulnerability have little explanatory power. The evidence suggests that non-Gaussian synchronicity primarily reflects common upside optionality rather than common downside vulnerability.

title: Interrupting Sovereign Debt Payments to Enforce Judgments: Nuisance or Real Threat?
affiliations: and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Interrupting Sovereign Debt Payments to Enforce Judgments: Nuisance or Real Threat?
detail.abstract: This article examines an increasingly prominent, yet underexplored, sovereign debt enforcement strategy: the use of judicial processes to interrupt payments to third-party creditors in order to satisfy sovereign debt judgments and arbitral awards. Rather than pursuing traditional execution against sovereign assets, judgment creditors have sought to restrain, attach, or otherwise disrupt payment flows associated with performing debt instruments, thereby increasing pressure on sovereigns to settle outstanding claims. On the one hand, payment disruption efforts frequently fail to survive on the merits due to immunity protections, ownership requirements, and contractual barriers that limit creditors’ ability to reach payment flows. On the other hand, even unsuccessful actions can generate significant leverage by creating uncertainty, threatening payment disruptions, and increasing the risk of default, rating downgrades, and reputational harm. The article reviews a series of such enforcement attempts under New York law, highlighting how turnover orders, restraining notices, injunctions, and related remedies have been deployed in practice. It concludes by evaluating legislative, contractual, and institutional reforms that could reduce systemic risks posed by payment-interruption tactics while preserving the enforceability of sovereign debt contracts.

title: State-Led Coercion and Popular Resistance: Evaluating Conflict Dynamics in Amhara and Oromia
affiliations: Bule Hora University

detail.title: State-Led Coercion and Popular Resistance: Evaluating Conflict Dynamics in Amhara and Oromia
detail.abstract: The contemporary political trajectory of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has been defined by severe security crises, characterized fundamentally by the collision between centralizing state-led coercion and decentralized popular resistance movements. This manuscript examines the structural, historical, and immediate political catalysts driving protracted armed conflict and civic contestation within the Amhara and Oromia regional states. Through an evaluation of federal military doctrine, the institutional degradation of multinational federalism, and the rise of localized insurgencies-most notably the Amhara Fano militias and the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA)-this paper analyzes the systemic implications of state-sanctioned crackdowns. Utilizing empirical event data, human rights monitoring reports, and sociopolitical frameworks, we argue that the Abiy Ahmed administration's reliance on kinetic solutions and state-of-emergency decrees has exacerbated ethnic polarization, institutional decay, and civilian displacement, threatening the foundational integrity of the Ethiopian state.

title: CEO Q&A Engagement and the Cost of Debt
affiliations: College of Charleston,  and

detail.title: CEO Q&A Engagement and the Cost of Debt
detail.abstract: We examine whether creditors price CEO engagement during earnings-call question-and-answer (Q&A) sessions, measured by the time CEOs spend speaking during Q&A. Using nonfinancial and nonutility S&P 1500 firms from 2015 through 2024, we find that firms with greater CEO Q&A engagement have lower corporate bond spreads. Consistent with an information-substitution channel, the relation weakens as analyst information production increases and is stronger when creditor information frictions are higher, including among firms with lower credit quality, lower institutional holdings, higher leverage, and greater analyst dispersion. Following large analyst coverage losses, firms with high pre-event CEO Q&A engagement experience smaller increases in bond spreads, by roughly 24 to 25 basis points, with no evidence of differential pre-trends. The results are robust to sample-selection concerns, single coverageloss events, and alternative CEO communication measures. These findings suggest that public debt markets price interactive managerial disclosure and that CEO Q&A engagement can substitute for analyst information production.

title: The Nexus between Energy Prices and the Real Exchange Rate in South Africa: Evidence from a Mixed Methods Approach

detail.title: The Nexus between Energy Prices and the Real Exchange Rate in South Africa: Evidence from a Mixed Methods Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Dear Editor I wish to submit a new manuscript entitled “The Nexus between Energy Prices and the Real Exchange Rate in South Africa: Evidence from a Mixed Methods Approach” for consideration by the SSRN. I confirm that this work is original and has not been published elsewhere nor is it currently under consideration for publication elsewhere. In this paper, I examined the nexus between energy prices and the Real effective exchange rate in South Africa. We further examine the effects of energy price shocks on a macroeconomic system, as well as the different monetary regimes suitable for macroeconomic stability during such shocks. This work is both timely and significant given the recent surge in energy prices resulting from geopolitical tensions. It will further enhance the South African Reserve Bank's ability to curb the effects of such a shock in the future. The paper should be of interest to readers in macroeconomics, statistical modelling, and energy economics. Please address all correspondence concerning this manuscript to me at nyatimc@tut.ac.za. Thank you for your consideration of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: The present study analyses the nexus between energy prices and the real exchange rate in South Africa. Explicitly, the study seeks to ascertain whether the South African Rand is an energy currency. Further, the study examines the long-run relationship between the real effective exchange rate and its fundamentals, viz., the terms of trade, the Balassa-Samuelson effect, the net foreign asset position, trade openness, the fiscal balance, and the real interest rate. Furthermore, the study provides model-based analysis of the macroeconomic and monetary policy effects of energy price shocks within four monetary policy regimes. To this end, the study applied an analytical approach integrating cointegration techniques and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) methods with a structural New Keynesian Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) framework. The findings of this study indicate that the South African Rand is an energy currency, as there is a long-run cointegrating relationship between energy terms of trade and the real effective exchange rate. The structural model results support the reduced-form econometric results and provide strong support for adopting an augmented Taylor rule that explicitly recognises external-sector dynamics, thereby strengthening monetary policy effectiveness and enhancing macroeconomic stability in an environment characterised by volatile global commodity prices and financial conditions.

title: Rational Expectations and Macroeconomic Policy
affiliations: Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics and Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics

detail.title: Rational Expectations and Macroeconomic Policy
detail.abstract: For decades, the macroeconomy was viewed as proceeding independently of the economy that individual households and firms experience.The ultimate benefit of the new policy scenario can be related to the expectations people form and how they act on these expectations. Households, for example, consume in anticipation of prices, workers work in anticipation of future wages, and firms invest in anticipation of future demand. For many years, economists resorted to explanations of expectations that relied exclusively on past experience. The “adaptive expectations hypothesis,” for instance, posited that people make forecasts by extrapolating from the past and then adjust those forecasts gradually as they make errors.The idea, encapsulated in J. F. Muth’s iconic 1961 paper "Rational Expectations and the Theory of Price Movements," placed expectations at the center of mainstream macroeconomics and finance for much of the next 40 years. Muth countered that economic agents use all available relevant information, including their understanding of how the economy works, to form their expectations.Rational people think ahead. People anticipate changes in economic policy. For this reason,an expected policy change may be reflected in prices and wages ahead of time, while an unexpected change may have a more powerful short-run impact on real economic activity.Muth’s argument was reinforced by Robert E.Lucas's development of the New Classical macroeconomics, so-called “Lucas Critique”,which showed that economic relationships estimated from past data may not hold firm when the policy environment shifts. Sargent and Wallace extended this argument, suggesting that expected, systematic monetary policy may be ineffective with respect to real output and employment.

title: Rapid Diffusion, Widening Inequality: Housing Position and Rooftop Solar Access in the Netherlands

detail.title: Rapid Diffusion, Widening Inequality: Housing Position and Rooftop Solar Access in the Netherlands
detail.abstract: Residential rooftop solar is expanding rapidly, but access to its benefits remains uneven across households. This study examines how income inequality in dwelling-level rooftop solar access evolved during rapid diffusion in the Netherlands and how this pattern is associated with housing position. Using Dutch Housing Survey data for 2018, 2021 and 2024, we analyze 124,703 household-dwelling observations. Access increased across all income groups, but much more strongly among higher-income households. By 2024, the gap between the highest and lowest income deciles reached almost 50 percentage points. After adjusting for socio-demographic and regional differences, adding housing-position variables reduced the adjusted income gap by roughly half. The findings suggest that equitable solar policy should address housing-based barriers alongside financial support and individual incentives.

title: Volatility Salience: Evidence from the Options Market
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong -Liverpool University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, CUHK Business School, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) - International Business School Suzhou and

detail.title: Volatility Salience: Evidence from the Options Market
detail.abstract: This paper examines how volatility salience affects option prices. We construct a volatility salience theory measure (VST) capturing the degree to which recent realized volatility deviations stand out from the market benchmark. Using U.S. equity option data, we show that high volatility salience leads to significantly lower delta-hedged option returns for both calls and puts, consistent with investors overweighting salient volatility shocks and bidding up implied volatility beyond fundamentals. The effect is distinct from the variance risk premium and other volatility-based measures and is amplified by limits to arbitrage, high sentiment, and retail participation. Our findings extend salience theory to the second moment of returns and provide direct evidence of its pricing implications in derivatives markets.

title: Interdisciplinary Theory of Value
affiliations: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

detail.title: Interdisciplinary Theory of Value
detail.abstract: This article presents an overview of the key concepts of an interdisciplinary approach to economic value theory. These concepts are discussed in more detail in Parts I–XIII of "Physical Macroeconomics," presented in the author's previous articles on SSRN. A central concept is the similarity (isomorphism) between economic value and Gibbs free energy—these quantities characterize the working potentials of socioeconomic and thermodynamic systems, respectively. This isomorphism is reflected in the two-component nature of economic value, which contains an objective energy component and a subjective information component. This article presents updated empirical data (up to 2024) confirming the two-component nature of economic value.

title: Broadcasting Activism: Evidence from the Civil Rights Movement

detail.title: Broadcasting Activism: Evidence from the Civil Rights Movement
detail.abstract: This paper examines how media shape social movements in the context of the U.S. Civil Rights Movement. I exploit quasi-random variation in television rollout from the 1948 FCC licensing freeze, and corroborate the estimates with a terrain-based measure of signal reception. Early access to television raised the average annual probability of a civil-rights protest between 1954 and 1968 by 6.9 percentage points, roughly 68 percent of the sample mean. The effect operated over two horizons. In the short run, television coordinated protest across localities around nationally salient events. I provide evidence that images contributed to this coordination, as the response was larger for events in which demonstrators and police clashed. In the long run, television deepened organizational capacity, doubling NAACP membership where a branch already existed, and shifted beliefs about Black residents' support for desegregation rather than respondents' own views.

title: Bringing Rights Home: Organizing, Law, and the Future of Domestic Workers' Rights

detail.title: Bringing Rights Home: Organizing, Law, and the Future of Domestic Workers' Rights
detail.abstract: Domestic work is one of the most under-valued and under-regulated labor sectors in the world. Characterized by the isolated and intimate nature of the work, often set in the private home, it is a labor sector rife with abuses, including wage theft, sexual harassment, and human trafficking. The sector employs a high proportion of immigrant workers, of varying immigration statuses, including the undocumented, creating further vulnerabilities. Despite the high risks and extremely poor conditions that many domestic workers face, the domestic work sphere has eluded government regulation and full protection under the traditional canon of U.S. labor statutes for nearly a century. And the criminal legal framework in place to prosecute violations of human trafficking law is neither preventative nor effective in addressing what would otherwise be considered labor rights violations that fall short of outright trafficking in persons in the domestic work sector. In the last decade, a movement has formed to advocate for the human and civil rights of domestic workers through state-level Domestic Workers Bills of Rights. However, these have never achieved broad impact on the federal level, and many of them are modest in the protections they provide, resulting in a patchwork system of only partial labor rights for domestic workers. This Article explores the historic challenges, common approaches, and emerging innovations in improving regulation of domestic work. It argues that labor organizing has been overlooked as an effective tool for reform. It identifies lingering gaps in U.S. legislation and international instruments, assesses the unique hurdles for immigrant domestic workers, and proposes a multi-faceted approach to reforming labor protections for domestic workers through domestic and international law. It considers legal scholarship on creating countervailing power among poor and working-class people to counter the increasing influence of corporations and the wealthy by pursuing organization-enabling legislation and applies it to the domestic work sphere. And it argues that the domestic worker movement currently has a range of untapped strategies for advocating for legal change. This Article explores these untapped strategies and argues that a combination of organizing, litigation, legislation, executive action, and international cooperation is needed to build supportive institutions to enforce the rights of domestic workers on the national stage.

title: Who Absorbs a School Day? School Schedules and Household Time Allocation

detail.title: Who Absorbs a School Day? School Schedules and Household Time Allocation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

Access to the microdata was authorized by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications under Article 33 of the Statistics Act (approval Sō-Tō-Sui No. 101, March 23, 2026).

detail.abstract: When a school day disappears, who absorbs it? This paper observes the complete same-day time accounts of children and both parents around Japan's transition to a five-day school week. Under the biweekly regime of 2001, the national time-use survey administratively assigned households to adjacent school and no-school Saturdays, shifting attendance by 40 percentage points; the identical calendar positions in 2006 provide a placebo after the full abolition of Saturday classes in 2002. Mothers' daily market work is a precise zero: equivalence tests reject effects larger than 11 minutes, or 0.06 of a control standard deviation. Children aged ten and older absorb the half-day instead—a child induced to attend loses 58 minutes of sleep, along with television and family time—while fathers work about 25 minutes more. Prefecture-level reduced forms scale with the local first stage while intercepts are indistinguishable from zero, consistent with an attendance channel. After abolition, the baseline comparison shows mothers' Saturday participation falling 4.1 percentage points relative to women aged 25–59 without coresident children under 16; exact age standardization leaves a similar 3.3-point reform-interval estimate with lower precision. School childcare is capitalized into standing arrangements that adjust over longer horizons rather than expressed through mothers' day-to-day labor supply.

title: Who Teaches High School Computer Science and Does It Matter?
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - College of Education

detail.title: Who Teaches High School Computer Science and Does It Matter?

declarations.funderStatement: The work was supported by the National Science Foundation [2317943]; Google Computer Science Education Research Program [93661913].

detail.abstract: Background and Context: High schools have rapidly increased the number of computer science (CS) courses they offer. One challenge for these expansions is staffing CS classrooms with qualified teachers. Objective: This study provides novel evidence about who teaches high school CS courses and what CS teacher attributes are important for ensuring that students have high-quality experiences in those courses. Method: This study uses statewide longitudinal student- and teacher-level data from North Carolina high schools in descriptive and regression-based analyses. Findings: CS courses are taught by teachers who are better qualified than teachers of other courses in terms of experience, education, and National Board Certification (NBC), though CS teachers often lack preparation to teach CS specifically. CS and non-CS courses have teachers with similar racial demographics, but CS courses are more likely to be taught by men. Teachers’ observable qualifications and characteristics are not consistently related to whether their students take or are successful on Advanced Placement (AP) CS exams. However, there is some evidence that teachers with more experience generally, more experience teaching CS, or NBC have better student outcomes. Implications: These findings suggest that stricter certification requirements for CS teachers may restrict CS course expansions unnecessarily, though they also point to important directions for future research on CS teacher quality.

title: Comparative Nutritional Assessment of Lentils (Lens culinaris Medik.) from Morocco and Spain: A Two-tier Multivariate Approach with Reference to Greek and Canadian Germplasm
affiliations: Hassan II University, Hassan II University of Casablanca and Hassan II University

detail.title: Comparative Nutritional Assessment of Lentils (Lens culinaris Medik.) from Morocco and Spain: A Two-tier Multivariate Approach with Reference to Greek and Canadian Germplasm
detail.abstract: Lentils (Lens culinaris) are a major source of plant protein and essential micronutrients, but statistically defensible data on mineral composition across production regions remain scarce. This study compares mineral composition in Moroccan and Spanish lentils through a two-tier data strategy. Tier 1 combines 36 individually analyzed Moroccan samples (18 landraces and 18 improved varieties, 2014-2015 harvests, ICP-AES) with cultivar-level data for six Spanish cultivars (Plaza et al., 2021) for formal inferential statistics. Welch's t-tests showed significantly lower iron (5.28 ± 2.73 vs. 12.52 ± 1.99 mg/100 g DM, p < 0.001) and significantly higher magnesium (113.14 ± 16.84 vs. 92.48 ± 7.80 mg/100 g DM, p < 0.001) in Moroccan than Spanish lentils, with no significant difference in calcium (p = 0.254). Principal component analysis on Ca, Fe and Mg separated the two origins mainly along an iron-driven axis (PC1 + PC2 = 89.0% of variance). Tier 2 situates these findings within a broader geographic context using literature-reported reference ranges for Greece (Tziouvalekas et al., 2022) and Canada (Vargas et al., 2025), without inferential testing given data heterogeneity. The findings show pronounced geographic variability in lentil mineral profiles and support transparent, level-appropriate statistical treatment when combining secondary data sources.

title: Are Firms' and Governments' Emission Reduction Commitments Aligned? The European Case
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Financial Markets Group,  and University of Finance - Marketing

detail.title: Are Firms' and Governments' Emission Reduction Commitments Aligned? The European Case
detail.abstract: Drawing on more than 89,000 firm-level observations from 94 countries across Europe, other advanced economies, Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East, sourced from the World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, we examine whether ambitious national climate commitments translate into greater corporate adoption of CO2 monitoring and energy management practices. The results show that an ambitious national net zero target, defined as 2050 or earlier, compared with a later or no target, is associated with a statistically significant increase in corporate climate mitigation action once firm-level characteristics and country fixed effects are considered. When we focus on Western European countries with net-zero targets of 2050 or earlier, the positive effect is larger and remains statistically significant, especially for energy management practices. Firms with audited financial reports are the most likely to adopt these measures, while SMEs are the least likely. A regional disparity also emerges: firms in Eastern European countries outside the European Union (EU) that have experienced climate-related physical events with economic consequences are the most likely to adopt energy management measures. By contrast, firms in energy-intensive sectors in the same Eastern European countries, mainly industry and transport, are less likely than their EU peers to adopt these practices and show substantially lower probabilities of adopting climate measures.

title: The Dual Exposure Paradox: Crude Export Dependency, Refinery Deficiency, and the Structural Limits of Household Cost Insulation in Oil-Producing Developing States

detail.title: The Dual Exposure Paradox: Crude Export Dependency, Refinery Deficiency, and the Structural Limits of Household Cost Insulation in Oil-Producing Developing States

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No special interest to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: no funding was received for thisresearch work.

detail.abstract: Oil-producing developing states, such as Nigeria, Venezuela, among others are conventionally expected to benefit from rising global crude prices. This paper argues that states which simultaneously lack adequate domestic refining capacity and have removed fuel subsidies face a structurally perverse outcome: government revenues improve while household welfare deteriorates within the same price shock. We term this the dual exposure paradox: a mechanism which is inadequately captured by existing resource curse and Dutch Disease frameworks, which focus on currency appreciation and deindustrialisation rather than the refinery gap as a welfare transmission channel. Drawing on Nigeria’s energy sector between 2022 and 2026; a period spanning the removal of fuel subsidies, the partial commissioning of the Dangote refinery, and the 2026 global energy shock triggered by conflict in the Persian Gulf, the paper develops a conceptual framework linking crude price movements, refining dependency, deregulated downstream markets, and household fuel cost exposure. We situate Nigeria within a comparative analysis of Angola, Venezuela, and Indonesia to identify the structural and policy conditions under which the paradox intensifies or resolves. The findings in the paper suggest that subsidy removal, while fiscally necessary, functions as an amplification mechanism that accelerates the transmission of global crude price volatility to domestic pump prices in refinery-deficient economies. The paper concludes that domestic refinery investment, rather than subsidy policy alone  is the primary structural remedy available to such states, and that this insight carries significant implications for energy policy design across sub-Saharan Africa and other refinery-poor oil producers.

title: Colonial and Anti-Colonial Discourses of Peace in Ukraine
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Government, City University London - Department of International Politics and University College London

detail.title: Colonial and Anti-Colonial Discourses of Peace in Ukraine
detail.abstract: This article analyses competing discourses of peace in the Russo-Ukrainian war by asking how they reproduce, enable, or resist relations of colonial domination. It examines peace proposals advanced by Russia, Ukraine, and aspiring mediators, in particular, Trump's diplomatic blitz and the Group of Friends for Peace on the Ukraine Crisis, founded by China and Brazil at the UN. We argue that these peace discourses are structured by three competing logics: Russia's colonial entitlement, mediators' colonial enablement, and Ukraine's anti-colonial resistance. Russia framed peace as a pacification of an allegedly chaotic Ukraine in a great-power concert with the US, demanding limits on Ukraine's internal and external sovereignty. The Trump administration and the China-Brazil initiative did not fully reject these premises: they treated Ukrainian concessions as a route to stability and validated spheres-of-influence thinking. Ukraine articulated peace as sovereign agency and justice, advancing a distinct variety of anticolonialism that rejected self-victimisation and sought alignment with European modernity. By reframing peace discourses as sites of colonial politics and extending existing accounts of anticolonial agency, the article contributes to the scholarship on wartime diplomacy, the normative foundations of multipolarity, and varieties of anti-colonialism.

title: The Last Bin: Match Termination and the Illusion of Within-Match Effects in Sports

detail.title: The Last Bin: Match Termination and the Illusion of Within-Match Effects in Sports
detail.abstract: A large class of sports ends the match at the very outcome that within-match event studies are built to explain. In that class, a random number generator run through the standard two-way fixed-effects specification produces an event study with clean pre-trends and a discontinuity of +5.6 percentage points (t = 32.9) on 8,351 UFC bouts, and its analogues in tennis, hockey, and judo. We characterize the artifact exactly: the expected estimator under the null is a computable functional of the data, verified against permutation distributions to hundredths of a permutation standard deviation across eight panels. Its sign is determined by how the studied outcome relates to match termination-terminal outcomes inherit inflation, nonterminal outcomes deflation, continuation-conditioned outcomes deflation-and for purely terminal outcomes we prove the design is not biased but empty: the stratified permutation null is degenerate at the observed statistic, so no within length treatment signature exists. Re-analyzing the 2023-Wimbledon momentum wave on its own dataset, the affirmative findings-streak tests, index-winner associations, non-random fluctuations-are reproduced in full by momentum-free simulation of the sport's rules, with the residual at scale slightly negative. We provide a zero-cost diagnostic, exact null means in place of simulated ones, and remedies stated with their estimands.

title: Principal-agent Problems in the Governance of a Mars Settlement
affiliations: University of Central Florida

detail.title: Principal-agent Problems in the Governance of a Mars Settlement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: A permanent Mars settlement would likely be nanced and supplied from Earth while being operated by settlers who possess much of the local knowledge and control needed to keep it alive. This article analyzes that relationship as a principal-agent problem. It argues that physical separation from Earth, dependence on survivalcritical infrastructure, and local knowledge would make substantial Martian autonomy unavoidable. Yet this same autonomy would create agency risks, including strategic reporting, mission drift, and ex post bargaining over Earth-nanced assets. The article also considers the internal danger that control over survival-critical systems could become political power within the settlement. Rather than treating Earth control or Martian independence as the only options, it evaluates institutional responses that structure autonomy through incentives, credible information, transition rules, and divided control over critical systems. The central governance challenge is designing institutions that preserve cooperation as Martian self-suciency increases and Earth's practical control declines.

title: AAPL versus MSFT: A Comparative Empirical Analysis of Return, Volatility, and Co-movement, 2020-2026

detail.title: AAPL versus MSFT: A Comparative Empirical Analysis of Return, Volatility, and Co-movement, 2020-2026
detail.abstract: This paper presents an exploratory, beginner-level empirical comparison of Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) common stock over the period January 2, 2020 to August 21, 2026. Using daily adjusted closing prices obtained through the yfinance data interface, the study examines total return, full-period daily return volatility (measured by standard deviation), 30-day rolling volatility, the Pearson correlation coefficient between the two stocks' daily returns, and a simple return-to-volatility ratio. Over the sample period, AAPL generated a total return of approximately 328.04 percent, compared with 218.88 percent for MSFT. Measured across the full sample as a single figure, AAPL exhibited marginally higher daily volatility (1.98 percent) than MSFT (1.92 percent). However, an examination of rolling volatility over time indicates that this ranking was not stable: MSFT's 30-day volatility rose to approximately 3.31 percent by the end of the sample period, exceeding AAPL's contemporaneous value of approximately 2.05 percent, despite MSFT's lower average volatility over the full period. The two return series exhibit a moderately strong positive correlation of 0.6400. AAPL produced the higher return-to-volatility ratio (165.76 versus 114.04 for MSFT). The paper concludes that AAPL was the strongerperforming security over the period studied, while noting that the relative risk ranking between the two stocks depended materially on whether risk was measured as a single full-period average or as a time-varying series. The analysis is explicitly presented as a beginner-level empirical exercise and does not claim methodological novelty; its contribution is a transparent, reproducible walkthrough of standard descriptive techniques applied to a specific, well-defined sample.

title: Designing Circular Infrastructure for Large-Scale Dryland Agricultural Expansion: A Project-Status-Adjusted Assessment of Biogas, Biochar, Water and Nutrient Pathways in Algeria
affiliations: , University of Science and Technology of Oran Mohamed Boudiaf (USTO-MB) and University of Sciences and Technology Houari Boumediene

detail.title: Designing Circular Infrastructure for Large-Scale Dryland Agricultural Expansion: A Project-Status-Adjusted Assessment of Biogas, Biochar, Water and Nutrient Pathways in Algeria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests affecting this manuscript. No company funded, commissioned or participated in the research, and no non-public company information was used.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses peer-reviewed literature and publicly available sources and does not involve human participants, patient data, animal experiments or interviews.
